articles.title: Fantasy Football Stock Report: Chargers' offense looks lost while Panthers' unit continues to thrive going into Week 3
articles.summary: Matt Okada takes you through the biggest risers and fallers after Week 2 for fantasy football.
articles.body:
As I write this on Sunday night, 15 of 16 Week 2 games are in the books (with Monday night remaining) and the season's second week looked ... completely different from its first. There were promising improvements, concerning trends and performances that changed our early outlook on players and teams. As always, some of these shifting perspectives will have permanent ramifications in fantasy football.

With that in mind, I've compiled another full fantasy stock report. These are the most notable risers and fallers heading into Week 3.

Frankly, Dalton Kincaid isn't just the top "Stock Up" player of this week. He's arguably the top "Stock Up" player in all of fantasy, relative to his summer draft price. He's made a legitimate two-week case as the top tight end behind Trey McBride and Brock Bowers (when he's eventually healthy). After a monster 130-yard performance in Week 1, Kincaid caught seven of eight targets for 95 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 on TNF.

Most importantly, he tied Keon Coleman for the most routes on the team (26), the nail in the coffin of years of previously head-scratching usage in Buffalo. That full-time usage now unlocks what has always been elite efficiency for the Bills tight end — since he was drafted in 2023, Kincaid's 2.0 yards per route run is second to George Kittle among all tight ends with 300+ routes. Kincaid is one of the best weapons for the league's best quarterback in what is almost certainly the league's best offense. He's an elite fantasy asset, period, full stop.

The second game of the post- A.J. Brown era revealed a version of DeVonta Smith we certainly didn't see in Week 1 and have rarely seen before. The Eagles' No. 1 receiver saw 13 targets — a 38% share — and caught 10 of them for 117 yards and a touchdown. That tied Smith's previous career high in targets (from the 2022 season) and matched his second-best reception total, positioning him to be a top-five scoring wideout on the week entering Monday Night Football. But perhaps most importantly, he looked the part throughout the game, making a number of true WR1 catches, most notably this snag with the game on the line on third down, to set up the walk-off score. Smith has a juicy matchup with the Bears in Week 3, where he could cement his place as a high-end WR2 with another performance like Sunday's.

It was a near-perfect storm for TreVeyon Henderson as he returned from a Week 1 injury absence. Running mate Rhamondre Stevenson coughed up another troubling fumble, Henderson ripped off an explosive 39-yard touchdown run and the volume split finished 16 touches to seven in the younger back's favor. Stevenson has now fumbled 18 times since he was drafted in 2021, most by any non-QB in the entire NFL .

Considering how much more explosive and effective Henderson has looked as a runner, this trend could threaten to relegate Stevenson to pass-protection snaps and a complementary receiving role. That would give Henderson an open lane to RB1 usage in what should be a great offense (though Drake Maye and Co. have seemed a little wobbly to start the season). Henderson isn't a locked-and-loaded RB2 yet ... but another game or two like this one and he'll be there quick.

Jaylen Waddle & Jonah Coleman , WR/RB, Broncos

While these two "Stock Ups" are largely unrelated — outside of being on the same team — I'm combining them here for efficiency! Let's start with Waddle. Outside of an absurdly disappointing two-yard season opener that had fantasy drafters in shambles, Waddle rebounded to the tune of eight catches for 138 yards on 10 targets against the Jaguars. He was targeted on 42% of the routes he ran in this game and snagged a 49-yard catch that landed him on the one-yard line ... inches away from an extra 6 fantasy points. Waddle's back in WR2 range after what will likely be remembered as an aberrant Week 1.

As for rookie running back Jonah Coleman, he took over when J.K. Dobbins exited with a hamstring injury — as RJ Harvey was inactive with his own hamstring injury — and took his 13 opportunities for 58 yards and a goal-line rushing touchdown. You might remember Coleman from the All-Sleeper Team two weeks ago, where I highlighted the potential he has to simply take the job in Denver . The door is creaking open, and it wouldn't be surprising to see the rookie atop the depth chart in the very near future.

To put it simply, the entire Panthers offense looks great coming off a 34-3 trouncing of the rival Falcons . Bryce Young followed a 361-yard, four-TD performance against the Bears in the opener with a 287-yard, three-TD encore on Sunday. He's second in the NFL in passing yards (to Tyler Shough ), has a 113.3 passer rating and has thrown six touchdowns to just one interception. And it's thanks in large part to his finally dangerous receiving corps, as Tetairoa McMillan hit 101 yards in Week 2, while Jalen Coker raised his season totals to 16 catches for 204 yards.

Plus, Chuba Hubbard caught a receiving touchdown for a second straight week (and has 151 yards on 27 touches) and tight end Darren Waller snagged two touchdown grabs of his own against Atlanta . Carolina's offense will face a real test next Sunday in Cleveland — after drawing the Bears and Falcons the first two weeks — but Young and Co. look extremely improved on tape and in the stat sheet. After two-and-a-half to three years of mostly mediocrity, it appears they've finally arrived.

The Chargers lost 26-14 to the Cardinals in Week 1, a team that had three wins last season. But that couldn't happen again in Week 2, right? Welp. They lost 26-14 to the Raiders , another three-win team from a season ago. No, I'm not joking. They made the kind of history you never want to make, and Justin Herbert looks completely lost in Mike McDaniel's offense.

Through two weeks, Herbert has thrown two touchdown passes and three interceptions , not to mention the three fumbles he committed on Sunday alone (none of which, miraculously, were recovered by Las Vegas ). The Chargers only reached the red zone twice in Week 2, with nine of their 13 drives ending in their own territory (including a game-ending safety). Ladd McConkey was surprisingly active for the game, but had just three targets and 5.0 fantasy points, while Quentin Johnston totaled one catch for seven yards on his five targets. Los Angeles is going to have some serious soul-searching to do before a terrifying matchup with the Bills in Week 3 ... but until the Chargers find whatever they're looking for, Herbert and his receivers could be very tough to trust.

A week after everything went right for the Bears in Week 1 ... absolutely nothing did in Week 2. They scored just three points against the Vikings and Caleb Williams suffered a hamstring injury that seemed severe when it went down . We're still waiting on the timeline and long-term impact of that injury, and Tyson Bagent is a serviceable backup, but it has not looked great for Rome Odunze , Luther Burden III or Colston Loveland either way.

Odunze has just five catches on seven targets this season, despite running essentially all the routes. Burden's usage has been disappointing and he's shown no sign of the breakout many had expected entering the season. And Loveland ... oof. The TE3 in draft ADP has one catch for three yards on five targets through two weeks. Tight ends with more fantasy points so far include Will Kacmarek and Jake Briningstool (Yes, those are real people). Stay tuned for the Williams news — and for future games in better weather against softer defenses — but the fact that Kalif Raymond is the top fantasy pass-catcher on this team is not great news for managers.

The optimistic perspective on Drake Maye after two weeks is that the early struggles can be blamed on the loss of A.J. Brown — after planning the offense around his acquisition — and that Maye will rebound on his return. But Brown or no Brown, it's pretty hard to explain Maye's one TD pass and four interceptions through two games. In all of 2025, Maye threw for fewer than 210 passing yards just three times. He's already done so twice in two games in 2026.

This week against Pittsburgh , he completed just 14 passes, was sacked three times and posted a 75.6 passer rating. He's sitting at just 21.8 fantasy points after Week 2, barely ahead of Aaron Rodgers and behind Jacoby Brissett , Cam Ward and Carson Wentz , among others. Maye could get into a barn-burner against the Jaguars next week, so you're probably still starting him (and hoping) for at least another couple games. But, right now, we are simply not seeing the breakout quarterback who led the Patriots to 14 wins last season.

With the elbow injury to Jayden Daniels — who does not have a timeline yet as I write this on Sunday night — I was initially tempted to "Stock Down" the entire Washington offense, or at least their entire receiving corps. However, I think the move to Marcus Mariota , for however long it lasts, is more specifically concerning for Terry McLaurin. For one thing, McLaurin has already not looked like the team's clear WR1 through two games: he has fewer targets (13) than Stefon Diggs (15), while Diggs (9), Rachaad White (8), Antonio Williams (7) and Dyami Brown (4) all have as many or more catches than McLaurin (4). McLaurin has an abysmal 30.8% catch rate and has honestly become something of an Alec Pierce , with high route participation and an incredibly high aDOT (14.4 air yards), but very little (if any) reliability. Mariota will take occasional downfield shots but is not going to be the solve for McLaurin's efficiency problems. And while Diggs can find relative consistency in a PPR role in the meantime — and caught a 20-yard touchdown from Mariota on Sunday — I worry McLaurin will be incredibly hit-or-miss for the foreseeable future.

A week after going berserk with three touchdowns in his Texans debut, David Montgomery totaled 10 rushing yards on six carries and finished Week 2 with 3.4 fantasy points. And while the Bengals' defense looks much improved, there's very little excuse or silver lining in 1.7 yards per carry amid a blowout loss. Worst of all, Woody Marks actually outcarried Montgomery eight to six ... though he was, incredibly, even less efficient, with just eight yards on those eight carries.

Unfortunately, the reality with Montgomery is that he'll probably mix-and-match these types of outings all year. When he finds the end zone, he'll be a strong RB2. When he doesn't, and particularly when the Texans fall behind, he'll likely have a series of fantasy duds. Montgomery thrived with his particular skill set when playing for the Lions' high-scoring, ever-in-the-red-zone offense. The Texans are not that. And it's going to reflect poorly in the running back's box score throughout the year.

articles.title: Michael Jordan retired 23 years ago, Tiger Woods barely plays, yet they still out-earn even Ronaldo and remain the highest-earning athletes in sports history
articles.summary: International Sports News: Michael Jordan retired 23 years ago and Tiger Woods rarely competes, yet both remain the highest-earning athletes in sports history, ahead of Cristiano Ronaldo and today’s biggest stars.
articles.body: Michael Jordan has been away from professional basketball since 2003, while Tiger Woods has spent years appearing only intermittently in competitive golf and has not officially retired. Neither is producing the kind of sporting income associated with the world's biggest active stars, yet both remain above them on the all-time earnings list.How Jordan and Woods stayed ahead without having to competeMichael Jordan has not stepped onto an NBA court in twenty-three years, and Tiger Woods has spent the better part of the last decade managing injuries rather than chasing majors, and yet neither man has been overtaken at the top of sport's all-time earnings ledger. According to Sportico's latest ranking of career earnings through the end of 2025, adjusted for inflation, Jordan sits first with $4.5 billion, Woods follows at $2.88 billion, and only then does the list arrive at Cristiano Ronaldo, the highest-paid athlete still competing, at $2.52 billion. LeBron James and Lionel Messi round out the top five, both of them still playing at the highest level, both of them still a considerable distance behind two men whose competitive careers effectively ended long ago.What makes this year's numbers worth pausing over is not simply that Jordan remains on top, since he has occupied that position for years, but that the gap separating him from Woods grew rather than shrank, expanding from roughly $850 million a year earlier to about $1.31 billion now, a jump of some $460 million in the space of twelve months. Two athletes who no longer need to compete are, in some sense, still winning.A Fortune That No Longer Depends on the ScoreboardThere was a period, decades ago now, when Jordan and Woods earned their fortunes the conventional way, by being unmistakably the best at what they did and letting the money follow the performance. Jordan built his early reputation on championships with the Chicago Bulls, and Woods built his on a run of major titles that reshaped what golf could commercially become, and in both cases the athlete and the business around him grew together during those years.Their playing careers have since slowed dramatically, Jordan's ending outright in 2003 and Woods's fading into sporadic, injury-interrupted appearances rather than a formal retirement, and yet the businesses attached to their names kept expanding well past the point where either man could carry them through performance alone.Jordan's estimated earnings for 2025 alone came to $275 million, a figure that quietly exceeded what Ronaldo made over the same period despite Ronaldo still playing at an elite level for Al-Nassr, and it also came to roughly twice the $137 million earned by Canelo Alvarez, who ranked second among active athletes for the year. None of that money arrived through a late-career contract or a surprise return to competitive basketball. It arrived through a business relationship that Jordan signed into as a twenty-one-year-old rookie, one that has since grown so large that its continued output no longer has anything to do with whether Jordan ever plays basketball again.The Deal Nike Almost Walked Away FromNike's original agreement with Jordan, signed in 1984 before he had appeared in a single professional game, was worth $2.5 million over five years and included a base salary of $500,000 annually, roughly three times what other NBA players were getting from shoe companies at the time.Buried inside that contract was a clause allowing Nike to exit the deal entirely if Jordan's shoes failed to generate $4 million in sales, a provision that reveals how uncertain the whole arrangement looked at the outset. Nike was, by most measures, an odd choice for a rising basketball star to align himself with, given that Adidas was generating about fifty per cent more revenue at the time, Reebok was closing in fast enough to overtake Nike by 1987, and Converse already had the league's biggest names, including Magic Johnson, Larry Bird and Julius Erving, wearing its shoes.What separated Jordan's contract from those of his contemporaries was a cut of sales built into the terms, meaning that as the shoes sold, his earnings grew alongside them rather than stopping at a fixed salary. Those shoes went on to generate more than $100 million in their first year alone, and the business built on that foundation has continued compounding for four decades, with the Jordan Brand pulling in $7.3 billion in revenue for the fiscal year ending May 2025, even after a sixteen per cent decline during a turnaround led by Nike's chief executive Elliott Hill.Woods, working in a different sport but along a strikingly similar path, spent twenty-seven years under a Nike deal of his own before the partnership ended in 2024, since which time he has built out sponsorships with Rolex, TaylorMade and Monster Energy, alongside ventures spanning golf technology, entertainment, course design and real estate through companies like TMRW Sports, PopStroke and Full Swing, the last of which was acquired by Versant Media Group for approximately $530 million in a deal completed this past August.What the Trophies Actually Bought ThemWoods's competitive record, set against his financial one, tells an unusual story about where professional golf's money actually sits. He has won 82 PGA Tour events and 15 major championships across his career, yet his tournament prize money adds up to only about $121 million, a modest figure next to the nearly $2 billion Forbes estimates he has earned pretax since turning professional.His last major victory came at the 2019 Masters, an improbable comeback at forty-three years old after an eleven-year gap between titles, and his most recent completed PGA Tour event was the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon, where he missed the cut entirely. He did appear at the TGL Finals in March 2026, representing Jupiter Links GC, only to be involved in a rollover car accident three days later that forced him away from the game once again while he recovers from an Achilles tendon rupture sustained the previous year and a seventh back surgery completed in October 2025.Jordan's situation involves no comparable physical setback, simply the passage of twenty-three years since he last competed professionally, and yet Q Scores data cited by Sportico found his public awareness rating still sits at 78 per cent, the highest of any athlete surveyed, with Woods following at 70 per cent alongside Serena Williams, and Shaquille O'Neal and Tom Brady trailing slightly behind at 75 and 73 per cent respectively. Jordan's likability score came in at 28, the highest recorded among the athletes surveyed, while Woods scored 11, actually below the average for sports personalities generally, a gap that suggests the two men's continued earning power rests on different foundations even as their financial outcomes look remarkably similar.A List Built on What Happens After the Applause StopsLooking across the full ranking rather than just its top two names, the broader pattern becomes harder to ignore. David Beckham, Roger Federer and Tom Brady each earned more than $50 million in 2025 through commercial arrangements alone, despite none of them currently competing in their sports, and the top 50 athletes collectively have generated approximately $56.2 billion in inflation-adjusted earnings through the end of 2025, spanning ten different sports, with basketball contributing the most names at 13, followed by golf with eight and boxing with seven.Only 18 of the 50 athletes on the list remain actively competing, and 20 have crossed the billion-dollar threshold in career earnings, with the cutoff for inclusion sitting around $595 million, a mark currently held by the retired Formula 1 driver Kimi Räikkönen.Serena Williams remains the only woman to appear anywhere on the list, with approximately $680 million in career earnings, and perhaps most tellingly, not a single athlete under the age of 30 has made the cut at all, a gap that seems likely to close given how dramatically on-field salaries and endorsement markets have grown for the current generation.Ronaldo, James and Messi continue adding to their totals every year they keep playing, chasing performance bonuses and new contracts the way athletes always have, while Jordan and Woods sit above them having already crossed into a different category entirely, one where the money keeps arriving regardless of whether either man ever plays again. Jordan stopped being merely a basketball player a long time ago, and it is that transformation, more than anything he ever did on a court, that keeps his name at the very top of a list built to measure exactly this kind of staying power.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Giants without Deonte Banks; Puka Nacua won’t play Monday for Rams
articles.summary: Giants will be short-handed at cornerback; Aaron Donald will play for Rams.
articles.body:
The New York Giants will be without starting cornerback Deonte Banks in Monday night's matchup with the Los Angeles Rams . Star wide receiver Puka Nacua won't play for the Rams.

Banks has a calf injury. He was listed as questionable, but did not practice Friday or Saturday. Nakua was an All-Pro last season, catching 129 passes.

The Giants also put cornerback Paulson Adebo on injured reserve last week. Linebacker Micah McFadden (neck) is also inactive.

Second-year defensive tackle Darius Alexander is also inactive. The Giants added veteran nose tackle Josh Tupou to the 53-man roster last week.

Star defensive tackle Aaron Donald is active for what will be his first NFL game since retiring at the end of the 2023 season.

articles.title: Nuggets rumors: The honest truth about Nikola Jokic's future in Denver
articles.summary: While one NBA analyst is questioning All-Star Nikola Jokic’s future with the Denver Nuggets, another believes it’s secure regardless of how the 2026-27 seaso...
articles.body:
While one NBA analyst is questioning All-Star Nikola Jokic 's future with the Denver Nuggets , another believes it's secure regardless of how the 2026-27 season develops. Jokic is expected to sign a historic extension with the Nuggets in 2027, which is why it's hard to fathom him signing elsewhere.

Jokic will be eligible for a whopping five-year, $359.5 million extension next summer , which should keep him with the Nuggets, as ESPN's Brian Windhorst noted, per The Hoop Collective podcast.

"Eastern European players, they don't have a history of plotting to exit in free agency," Windhorst said. "Those players typically like the teams that they grow up with. Even Giannis , Giannis is Greek. I think if all things are equal, Giannis wanted to stay in Milwaukee . And part of the reason why it was so messy to get Giannis was that he didn't necessarily want to do it. I don't think Jokic wants to leave. His circle is outrageously small.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"At the same time, he knows all this. He understands. He's one of the smartest guys in the league. So, on one hand, if you're looking at this future Power Rankings and you're saying, boy, this is a tough spot, and you're looking at Jokic saying, is he really going to go into the back of his prime in this situation, we should plot to try to get him. At the same time, it just seems totally out of his character and personality to plot to get out of the situation."

Nikola Jokic and the Nuggets, who finished 18th on ESPN's Future Power Rankings, will have their work cut out for themselves amidst a competitive Western Conference, led by the defending champion San Antonio Spurs and the 2024 Finals champion Oklahoma City Thunder . Still, inking arguably the best player in the NBA to a long-term extension doesn't guarantee Denver will be a top team in the league, as ESPN's Dave McMenamin pessimistically noted.

"I take him at his word that it is purely a business decision, financially, to wait to sign his contract," McMenamin said. "However, in doing that, that still puts the Nuggets — you give him the contract, you don't let the best player in franchise history, one of the best players of this generation, go, if you can keep him — but their ability to build anything close to a contender with Jokic making the most money in the league, the highest salary in the league, it's going to be hard. Really hard.

"Especially with all their picks out the door. I don't see the Nuggets being a legitimate contender for the rest of Jokic's career."

The Nuggets, who lost Tim Hardaway Jr. and Peyton Watson via free agency this summer, will have to fill the void left in their respective absences at the wing position, as McMenamin pointed out.

"They lost their two best bench players in Hardaway, and Peyton Watson was a part-time starter, but they lost two key rotation players," McMenamin said. "With the money, Jokic has stated reasons for waiting and not signing the extension this summer. He wants to maximize the contract. It's literally the biggest contract in the history of the league."

With the option to sign a four-year, $278 million extension over the summer, Nikola Jokic choosing the more lucrative offer in 2027 isn't out of the norm for a three-time MVP looking to maximize his dollars four years removed from leading the Nuggets to a championship in 2023.

With Denver's finances set up for the foreseeable future, the Nuggets have their core players, such as Jamal Murray and Aaron Gordon , locked in alongside Jokic, ESPN's Bobby Marks added.

"Well, they're the only team in the second apron. Jokic, of course, has a player option for next year," Marks said. "They're locked into that Aaron Gordon contract. Christian Braun is on that rookie extension, which is a big number. Cam Johnson could be a free agent, and Jamal Murray is on a max. You're basically top-heavy, and I think that shows you where your bench is. You're basically going to spend the minimum wheel every offseason."

Jokic, who finished second in MVP voting to Thunder's Shai Gilgeous-Alexander for the second season in a row, averaged 27.7 points on 56.9% shooting, including 38% from deep, also posted career-bests in rebounds (12.9), and assists (10.7) per game in 2025-26.

articles.title: Eagles bringing back fan favorite tight end Zach Ertz, AP sources say
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are bringing back fan favorite tight end Zach Ertz, three people familiar with the situation told The Associated Press.  Ertz will jo...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are bringing back fan favorite tight end Zach Ertz , three people familiar with the situation told The Associated Press.

Ertz will join the practice squad in hopes of shoring up a tight end room depleted by injuries, the people said Monday on condition of anonymity because the move had not been announced.

Ertz's return comes with multiple Eagles tight ends dealing with injuries.

Dallas Goedert is expected to miss several weeks with an MCL sprain suffered in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Tennessee Titans , one person told the AP. Backups Eli Stowers and Grant Calcaterra also are injured.

Ertz spent his first eight seasons with the Eagles, earning three Pro Bowl appearances, and made two key plays late in their Super Bowl win after the 2018 season. He played three seasons for Arizona after being traded in 2021 and spent the last two in Washington.

The 35-year-old suffered a torn ACL with the Commanders in December, but has been cleared to play.

Ertz is fifth on the NFL's career list for catches by a tight end with 825 and his 8,952 yards receiving are eighth. He's scored 57 touchdowns.

articles.title: Dodgers activate two key players immediately before big Padres series
articles.summary: The Dodgers can clinch a first-round postseason bye at home against the Padres
articles.body:
With one week left in the MLB regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are getting two key players back for a three-game home series against the San Diego Padres .

Pitcher Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages , who have been on the injured list since August, were activated from the injured list on Monday, an off-day for the Dodgers and Padres. The two National League West rivals can each clinch something important at Dodger Stadium — San Diego , a berth in the postseason, Los Angeles , a first-round bye.

Sasaki had a 3.05 ERA in seven starts post-All-Star-break when he developed a blister on his throwing hand in August. Pages played in his first All-Star Game in July, then fractured a bone in his right hand on Aug. 21, when he was hit by a 100.2 mph fastball from Pittsburgh Pirates starter Bubba Chandler .

The Dodgers managed to clinch the National League West without the two players, but both figure to play key roles in October for the defending World Series champions.

The Dodgers lost hard-throwing reliever Edgardo Henriquez to a back injury earlier this month . For all his second-half success as a starter, the Dodgers need Sasaki more in their bullpen as a right-handed compliment to left-handers Tanner Scott and Alex Vesia .

Pages, meanwhile, was excelling at the plate and in the field prior to his injury, which required surgery. He'll have six games to tune up for the postseason — and a chance at redemption for last October.

The Dodgers won the World Series even though Pages had only four hits in 16 postseason games, collecting an .078 batting average across four playoff rounds.

Without Pages, the Dodgers moved veteran utilityman Tommy Edman to center field. Through week's end, he was slashing .245/.328/.376 (94 OPS+) in 79 games this season.

The Dodgers are also expecting Shohei Ohtani to return during the Padres series, but he isn't eligible to be activated from the 15-day injured list before Wednesday.

In correpsonding 26-man roster moves, pitcher Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.

articles.title: Robert Wolk Spent 30 Years Racing at the Limit. Parking Lot Road Rage Killed Him.
articles.summary: Robert Wolk built a three-decade career out of deliberately running out of grip in controlled conditions, and he survived all of it. On Wednesday, 16 Septemb...
articles.body:
Robert Wolk built a three-decade career out of deliberately running out of grip in controlled conditions, and he survived all of it. On Wednesday, 16 September, he was killed on a suburban corner in Kempton Park at something close to walking pace, after a bump minor enough that he got out of his Audi to look at the damage. He was 41, he was on his way to the airport, and he had a race entry waiting for him in Cape Town.

Motorsport South Africa confirmed the death and described a career that ran from junior karting in the mid-1990s to a national touring car title in 2024. Sport, Arts and Culture Minister Gayton McKenzie, in a government statement issued on Saturday, called the killing "an act of senseless violence, on our roads." Three men were in custody by the end of that week.

What police say happened on Camwood Street

Gauteng police place the shooting at the corner of Camwood Street and Portland Drive in Esther Park, a quiet residential pocket of Kempton Park a short drive from OR Tambo International. According to police spokesperson Colonel Dimakatso Nevhuhulwi, Wolk's Audi was involved in a minor collision. He got out to assess and photograph the damage, an argument followed, a firearm was produced, and he was declared dead at the scene. A murder docket was opened, and the sequence was captured on CCTV, footage that has since been passed around social media by people who should know better. We are not linking it.

There is a bitter detail buried in that account. Photographing damage at the scene is exactly what every insurer, every broker and every fleet policy tells you to do. Wolk was following the script.

Three accused, and why a first appearance matters more than it looks

Police made one arrest on Thursday, 18 September, and two more on Friday, 19 September. The three men are aged between 24 and 33. A firearm and a vehicle were seized for forensic and ballistic work, and all three were due before the Kempton Park Magistrates' Court on Monday, 21 September, on a charge of murder.

A first appearance in South Africa is mostly procedural: charges are put, legal representation is sorted, and the matter is usually postponed for further investigation. The real fight is bail, and South African bail law is structured in a way most people outside the system do not appreciate. Murder is a Schedule 5 offence under the Criminal Procedure Act, which inverts the ordinary presumption and puts the burden on the accused to show that release serves the interests of justice. If the State alleges the killing was planned or premeditated, or that the accused acted in furtherance of a common purpose, the matter climbs to Schedule 6, where the accused must prove exceptional circumstances. With three men charged over one shooting, common purpose is on the table from day one.

Sentencing follows the same fork. Under the minimum sentencing regime introduced by the Criminal Law Amendment Act of 1997, murder that is premeditated or committed in execution of a common purpose carries life imprisonment as the prescribed starting point. Murder outside that bracket carries a 15-year minimum for a first offender, unless a court finds substantial and compelling reasons to go lower. Which is why the seized pistol matters so much: ballistics linking a specific weapon to the fatal round is usually what converts a group arrest into individual liability.

Wolk's record reads like three different drivers' careers stapled together. He took South African Junior GP karting titles in 1995 and 1997, collected multiple Formula Ford championships, won the SA Formula Volkswagen crown in 2013 and the SA Formula 1600 title in 2015, then went back-to-back in SA GTC in 2021 and 2022 before adding the SA Touring Cars championship in 2024. He received Junior Protea Colours in 1998 and Senior Protea Colours in 2022.

That spread is far harder than a list of trophies makes it look. Formula Ford and Formula 1600 are momentum cars: skinny tyres, almost no downforce, and a driving style built on refusing to scrub speed. Braking is a suggestion. GTC machinery is the opposite animal, a tube-frame silhouette racer wearing a showroom shell over a purpose-built chassis, with real aero load, real slick grip and a braking technique that punishes anyone still driving like a single-seater hero. Plenty of quick drivers cross that divide and look ordinary for a full season while they recalibrate. Wolk kept winning through the switch, in a national structure where testing budgets are thin and there is no simulator programme waiting to bail you out.

This was not a veteran winding down. In May he won his second King of the Hill title at the Simola Hillclimb in Knysna, an event run on roughly two kilometres of closed public road where the scenery consists of stone, banks and trees, one car goes at a time, and the margin for a misjudged entry is measured in centimetres. In June he came back to SA Touring Cars and won at Aldo Scribante outside Gqeberha. He was entered at Killarney International Raceway in Cape Town for the weekend of his death.

Circuit racing has spent a century engineering its way out of killing people, with barrier research, halo devices, fire suppression, extraction crews and medical response times that most public health systems would envy. It is not perfect, as the rescue of Ollie Millroy from a burning Ferrari in Shanghai made uncomfortably clear. But it is a system, and it improves every decade. None of it applies on a residential corner on a Wednesday morning.

The part every driver should actually take from this

South Africa's National Road Traffic Act sets out what you owe after a crash: stop, check for injuries and damage, give your name, address and vehicle particulars to anyone with a reasonable interest, and report the incident at a police station within 24 hours if those details were not exchanged. Nothing in that obliges you to conduct a roadside negotiation with a stranger, and nothing in it requires you to stand in the road while you do it.

If nobody is hurt, you are generally allowed to move the vehicles. Use that. If the other party's body language reads wrong, stay belted in with the doors locked, photograph through the glass, and drive to the nearest police station or a busy, well-lit forecourt to swap details there. A dual-channel dash cam with parking mode costs less than one panel respray and is the only witness that never changes its story. The pattern is depressingly consistent across jurisdictions, whether it is a drive-through queue dispute that ends with a fatal shooting , an Indianapolis confrontation that escalates in seconds , or a parking-lot argument that only ends well because of a steel-toed boot . The trigger is almost never the crash. It is the conversation afterwards.

There is an insurance wrinkle worth knowing too. The Road Accident Fund exists to compensate loss arising from the driving of a motor vehicle. A deliberate shooting that happens after a collision is a criminal act, not driving, so it generally falls outside that safety net entirely. Families in these cases are usually left with private life cover, whatever a civil claim against the accused might yield, and the cold reality that most defendants have nothing to attach. If you drive for a living or commute through high-risk corridors, that gap is an argument for checking the fine print on your personal accident and life cover rather than assuming the state backstop applies.

An empty slot on the Killarney entry list

Killarney's organisers had him on the entry for the weekend, and Motorsport South Africa's statement described a gap in the sport that will not be filled quickly. Both are true and neither is much comfort. South African national racing is a small, self-funded, tight-knit paddock where the same faces have been showing up with the same trailers for twenty years, and losing a two-time reigning hillclimb winner and a recent touring car champion is not an abstraction there. It is a missing car, a stalled team programme and a set of empty seats at scrutineering.

Motorsport has always asked its people to accept a level of risk that outsiders find irrational, and the sport has spent generations earning the right to make that risk smaller. Wolk had every reason to expect that the dangerous part of his week would begin at a green flag. Racing loses figures to illness and to age often enough, as it did with Lancia rally stalwart Alex Fiorio , and the paddock has learned how to absorb those. This is a different category of loss. He died standing still, on a public road, over a dented panel. Three men are now answering for it.

articles.title: Rams WR Puka Nacua inactive, Aaron Donald active for Giants visit on Monday night
articles.summary: All-Pro receiver Puka Nacua is inactive for the Los Angeles Rams' game against the New York Giants on Monday night due to a hip injury, while Aaron Donald is...
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. (AP) — All-Pro receiver Puka Nacua is inactive for the Los Angeles Rams ' game against the New York Giants on Monday night due to a hip injury, while Aaron Donald is active for the official start of his comeback .

Nacua is missing just the seventh game of his four-year career due to injury when the winless Rams host the unbeaten Giants at SoFi Stadium. He was added to the Rams' injury report on Friday with a hip problem, which is unrelated to the core muscle injury that limited him significantly during training camp and the preseason, according to coach Sean McVay.

Donald participated in team warmups before being declared active for his first NFL game since January 2024. The three-time AP NFL Defensive Player of the Year retired in March 2024 , but returned to the Rams late last month.

Donald didn't travel to Australia for the Rams' embarrassing season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers .

Receiver Jordan Whittington is also inactive for the Rams due to a quadriceps injury. The Rams, who frequently use three-tight-end offensive sets, will face the Giants with only four healthy wide receivers: Davante Adams , Xavier Smith , Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell .

Rams safety Kam Kinchens (hamstring) also is inactive.

The Giants' inactives included cornerback Deonte Banks (calf), who had four tackles in New York's season-opening win over Dallas , and linebacker Micah McFadden .

Running back Najee Harris is active for his Giants debut after being a healthy scratch last week. New York signed the four-time 1,000-yard rusher last month after an injury limited him to three games with the Chargers last season.

articles.title: WWE Raw Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights From September 21
articles.summary: On the heels of the performance of a lifetime in Mexico City, former No. 1 contender Penta was live Monday night on WWE Raw from San Antonio.
articles.body:
On the heels of the performance of a lifetime in Mexico City, former No. 1 contender Penta was live Monday night on WWE Raw from San Antonio.

What did the luchador have to say after pushing Roman Reigns to the limit?

Find out in this recap, which also includes grades and analysis from two different Money in the Bank Qualifying Matches and the latest showdown between Bayley and Lyra Valkyria.

Men's Money in the Bank Ladder Match : Dragon Lee vs. Solo Sikoa vs. Dominik Mysterio

Women's Money in the Bank Ladder Match : Iyo Sky vs. La Catalina vs. Roxanne Perez

Last Time in Action: Penta lost to Roman Reigns (Raw, September 14)

Penta kicked off Monday's show by addressing his loss to Roman Reigns and expressing his desire for a rematch for the World Heavyweight Championship.

Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh interrupted, with the former poking fun at the luchador's loss and claiming the fans in San Antonio wanted to hear from a winner from last week's show.

Penta claimed Rey Mysterio was the only real King of the Luchadors, instigating a brawl that ended with the heels bailing and the masked babyface standing tall.

Penta is as over as possible and now is absolutely the time to catapult him to the top of the card, even if that means not giving him the world title. Yet.

What a random segment between two guys who have not been involved with each other for several months. Smart money? Penta is somehow involved in the Money in the Bank Qualifying Match involving Dirty Dom later in the show.

Women's Money in the Bank Qualifier: Iyo Sky vs. La Catalina vs. Roxanne Perez

Last Time in Action: Roxanne Perez defeated Faby Apache, La Hiedra, and Nattie (AAA Triplemania, September 11); La Catalina defeated Flammer (AAA Triplemania, September 13); Iyo Sky and Sol Ruca defeated Perez and Raquel Rodriguez (Raw, August 10)

The Prodigy is headed to Money in the Bank after Roxanne Perez defeated Iyo Sky and AAA Reina de Reinas Champion La Catalina.

Perez outlasted her opponents in a highly competitive match, staying resourceful and alert as she avoided Sky's Over the Moonsault, which crashed into Catalina. Seizing the opening, she delivered Pop Rox and scored what has to be considered an upset win.

Long overshadowed as the third-most-prominent woman in the Judgment Day, she has seen her star rise again lately, earning a shot at Catalina's Reina de Reinas title at Worlds Collide and now heading to Money in the Bank for a guaranteed championship opportunity.

This was a huge spot for La Catalina, making her Raw debut against two of the best workers on the roster: Sky and Perez. It shows WWE officials have a lot of trust in her, even if her presence alongside The Prodigy was a nice way to build hype for their Worlds Collide match.

This was a fantastic match, featuring three women without any big story arcs, who managed to win over the fans in San Antonio with the action between the ropes. It was a fantastic night for all three, and they should be factored into more significant plans, regardless of the brand, moving forward.

Early Predictions for WrestleMania 43 Match Card 🔮

Last Time in Action: LA Knight and Solo Sikoa defeated The Usos (Raw, August 24)

On the heels of the official announcement from Raw general manager Adam Pearce that he will challenge Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship at Money in the Bank, Knight hit the ring to address the fans.

Focused and fired up all at the same time, Knight acknowledged Reigns' greatness while, at the same time, acknowledging that The OTC has never beaten him one-on-one, straight-up, and without any interference.

He vowed to head into New Orleans and leave with the World Heavyweight Championship.

This was as good as we have ever seen Knight on the mic in WWE. He was focused, spoke with intent, gave credit where it was due, but also hyped himself and his own feats up.

Crediting Reigns for winning on his own lately, while also calling him out for not doing the same when they clashed, lent credibility to his promo and set the stage for the Tribal Chief to have to prove him wrong at Money in the Bank.

Last Time in Action: Je'Von Evans defeated Big Cass and Austin Theory (Raw, September 14); Bron Breakker defeated Ethan Page and Rey Mysterio (Raw, September 7)

If you can't beat 'em, cause a disqualification to save face and avoid defeat.

That was the strategy The Vision employed in Monday's match between Evans and Breakker.

The Young OG had evaded every spear from The Badass, fended off all attempts at interference from Theory, Bronson Reed, Logan Paul, and Maxxine Dupri, and was still moments away from a huge upset win.

Until Theory re-entered the proceedings, broke up an OG Cutter, and drew the DQ.

After the match, The Vision teased a huge beatdown of the babyface, but Oba Femi returned, obliterated anyone in his way, and stood tall to close things out.

Evans defeated Breakker via disqualification

This was one of the best ways to present an underdog babyface we have seen in WWE in a long time. Evans was strong, confident, never fell for the same old heel tactics, and was on his way to actually winning while making The Vision look like fools. This was great stuff and went a long way in presenting the Young OG as a legitimate player at the next level.

The roof blew off the arena when Femi made the save. He is a monster Babyface at this point and someone who could win the world title today and be accepted in that role.

The Judgment Day Addresses the WWE Universe

JD McDonagh took exception to Joe Hendry's Funk Pop insult and claimed the nonsense has to end because it is affecting his family at home in Ireland.

Liv Morgan took over from there, turning her attention to the Women's World Championship, her controversial loss to Stephanie Vaquer in Chile, and what she calls the "Santiago Screwjob."

This brought out Becky Lynch, who appeared in the stands. She called B.S. on McDonagh's claims, said the whole world calls her the best referee ever, and staked her claim to a women's title opportunity.

La Primera joined the segment, promised to prove she didn't need Lynch to beat Morgan, and said she would defend against The Man, too.

She raised the women's title overhead to close things out.

This did not reinvent the wheel or anything, but it was efficient in that it highlighted two rivalries and continued to paint a picture of tension between Vaquer and Lynch, even as they focus their attention on common enemy, Morgan.

The inevitably Lynch vs. Morgan vs. Vaquer match is going to be hella great and a match with enough star power to justify a main event spot on a high-profile card.

Last Time in Action: Bayley lost to Lyra Valkyria (Saturday Night's Main Event, July 18); Valkyria lost to Sol Ruca in a match also involving Raquel Rodriguez (Raw, September 14)

Bayley started Monday's match seeking vengeance, unleashing months of frustration on Valkyria as the former tag team champions exploded.

A bum knee halted her momentum, though, and allowed the inaugural Women's Intercontinental Champion to seize control of the bout. The heel took control during the break and only relented when she missed a moonsault, allowing the Role Model to mount her comeback.

Bayley punished Valkyria and set up to drive her through the announce table, but the heel escaped. Stalking after her opponent like a predator after its prey, Bayley pummeled Valkyria inside the squared circle, but the referee's attempt to back her off backfired.

Valkyria used the momentary distraction to send her opponent into the ropes. A roll-up, with a handful of tights, secured the villainess the victory.

Bayley was deadly serious as she took to the squared circle, lacking her positive attitude or fiery demeanor. It was a welcome change of pace that underscored the gravity of the match.

The finish was clever, but without a stipulation (Loser Leaves WWE, maybe?), it feels like demand for the feud to continue has dropped sharply.

Hopefully, the company can stick the finish because, as the quality of the match here shows, Bayley and Valkyria are more than capable of delivering a match befitting them.

Last Time In Action: Roxanne Perez defeated La Catalina and Iyo Sky (Raw, earlier tonight); Lola Vice defeated Kelani Jordan and Raquel Rodriguez (Raw, September 14)

Adam Pearce introduced Vice not only as a competitor in Money in the Bank but also as the newest member of the Raw roster.

Before she could say much of substance, Perez interrupted.

A tense back-and-forth between former NXT foes ended with Vice standing tall.

This worked in that it introduced a first rivalry for Vice on the main roster, one that could see her stand beside Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch against The Judgment Day in the weeks to come.

Backstage, Bron Breakker informed Paul Heyman that the problem is not that Oba Femi is still breathing, but that he is.

Money in the Bank Qualifying Match: Penta vs. Dragon Lee vs. Dominik Mysterio

Last Time in Action: Dominik Mysterio and Liv Morgan lost to El Grande Americano and Stephanie Vaquer via DQ (Raw, September 14); Dragon Lee lost to Chad Gable (Raw, September 14); Penta lost to Roman Reigns (Raw, September 14)

After 946's Royce Keys, Bronco Nima, and Lucien Price kidnapped Solo Sikoa in front of a worldwide viewing audience as if there would be no legal repercussions, Adam Pearce announced that Penta would take the abducted Superstar's place in the men's ladder match qualifier.

The former No. 1 contender cashed his ticket to Money in the Bank following a thrilling, red-hot match-up that had fans in San Antonio hanging on every near-fall.

Late in the match, with Lee taken out of the equation following a Mexican Destroyer on the apron, Mysterio delivered a 619 and frog splash, but Penta kicked out. He dodged another 619, executed a springboard Mexican Destroyer, and picked up the win to the fans' delight as the show went off the air.

Bookending the show with Penta after his performance last week was an excellent creative decision.

Lee is red-hot right now and a Superstar the company should consider getting under a long-term contract sooner rather than later. He is just now finding his footing on TV and connecting with the audience based almost exclusively on his excellent work.

This was the best Mysterio in-ring performance in what felt like forever. Putting him there with the luchadores and letting him work from time to time, instead of playing a cowardly heel, may be exactly what the doctor ordered.

For the second consecutive week, Penta was the star of the show. WWE not only started and ended it with Cero Miedo, but the creative team also presented him in a way that told the world he is a top-tier performer with championship aspirations.

He delivered another stellar in-ring performance that sent fans home happy and excited about his current place in the WWE Universe.

Not quite the all-timer that last week's show was, this was still a really good episode of the flagship, highlighted by the excellent Money in the Bank qualifiers.

The steady storytelling involving The Bloodline and 946, the strength of the women's title picture, the introduction of a Vice-Perez feud, and a killer LA Knight promo really enhanced the viewing experience and made for another strong entry at a time of year when the product is typically on the colder side.

articles.title: 163 years before India-Japan T20I, cricket’s first match in Japan had revolvers behind the stumps
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: In the land of baseball, cricket is all set to score on Tuesday when India and Japan celebrate 75 years of diplomatic ties with a T20 International fo.
articles.body: In the land of baseball, cricket is all set to score on Tuesday when India and Japan celebrate 75 years of diplomatic ties with a T20 International for the Suzuki Cup at the petite Sano International Cricket Ground, about 80 km from Tokyo.It’s a historic occasion. But neither side is likely to be as tense and twitchy as those who played the first-ever cricket match in the Land of the Rising Sun in the summer of 1863. In that game, some players carried unusual protective gear: revolvers. The wicketkeeper would place his piece behind the stumps. The ground was guarded ‘by a small force armed with rifles’.Few cricket matches have been more nerve-wracking.Two British sides, the Navy and the Shore Team, the latter consisting of expatriates in Japan, faced off in the port town of Yokohama. Players were nervous because an attack from the sharp-sworded samurai was feared.Details of the strange but true incident came to light in 2012 following the efforts of dogged amateur British historian Mike Galbraith, who subsequently wrote about it in The Japan Times.While researching sports in Japan, Galbraith spotted the Wisden obituary of a British admiral, Sir Harry Rawson. The tribute said that he had played in the first cricket game in Japan. Further research led to an article in London-based ‘Cricket’ magazine written by James Campbell Fraser, the Shore Team’s skipper and a former Harrow student.In his article, Galbraith quoted Fraser: “It was a most novel sensation for the wicket-keeper, as he carried his revolver backwards and forwards from wicket to wicket and placed it behind the stumps.”Galbraith had earlier calculated that the match was played towards the end of June. However, he later discovered a naval officer’s diary, which led him to conclude that the game occurred over a month earlier.“The evidence shows that the match was played on or around May 12, 1863,” he said in an email response last week.In Japanese history, these were the final years of the shogunate, a period ruled by hereditary military governors. An incident in which bodyguards of a Japanese warlord had killed an English merchant had caused rage and bitterness. All foreigners were asked to leave the country by the end of June 1863.Galbraith said that the marines were sent to provide security cover for the expatriates and were stationed on the ships. However, no samurai attack occurred that day or later.The Navy team won. Fraser’s Shore men ‘got a jolly good lickin’.Five years later, the first cricket club in Japan was set up by Scottish tea merchant J P Mollison in Yokohama. But the sport didn’t take off; baseball did.Of late, though, cricket is finding its feet. According to the Japanese Cricket Association website, there are 7,300 players and about 14,000 annual participants in the Land of the Rising Sun.Japan’s greatest moment in the willow game came when the women’s team claimed bronze at the 2010 Asian Games.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Caitlin Clark’s rise in women’s basketball has brought plenty of attention to her growing profile off the court. One of the more unusual examples came through a box of cereal, as her Caitlin’s Crunch Time partnership with Hy-Vee turned a popular food product into a fundraising effort for young people.The campaign raised more than $100,000 for the Caitlin Clark Foundation, with the money supporting programmes centred on education, nutrition and sports across the Midwest. It offered fans a simple way to connect with Clark’s community work while supporting causes linked closely to her foundation. How did Caitlin Clark’s cereal campaign raise more than $100,000 for youth programmes?Per Caitlin Clark foundation website, the idea began as a partnership between Clark, her foundation and Hy-Vee. Caitlin’s Crunch Time cereal returned to Hy-Vee stores across the Midwest in May 2025 after an earlier limited release in Iowa. Hy-Vee pledged a percentage of the proceeds from each box sold to the Caitlin Clark Foundation.The partnership had a personal connection to Clark’s own story. Her foundation focuses on three areas: education, nutrition and sports, which it describes as pillars that played an important role in her development as an athlete. The cereal campaign gave fans a simple way to support that work while buying a product connected to Clark.“Having my own cereal is a fun way to connect with fans,” Clark said when Hy-Vee announced the 2025 release. She also thanked the company for supporting the foundation and its mission to improve the lives of young people.By Jan. 2026, the foundation announced that the campaign had raised more than $100,000. It said the funds would help support local initiatives across the Midwest, giving the campaign a purpose beyond the product itself.The partnership also forms part of a longer relationship between Clark and Hy-Vee. The foundation said the company had raised approximately $500,000 for its work through its partnership with Clark.Caitlin Clark’s $20M fortune is only one part of her story away from basketballClark’s commercial rise has been rapid since she became one of the biggest names in women’s basketball. Celebrity Net Worth currently estimates her net worth at $20 million and lists her 2026 WNBA salary at roughly $530,000. The site also reports that she earned about $16 million from endorsements in 2025 and has an estimated $28 million Nike deal running over eight years.Those figures show the scale of Clark’s success away from the basketball court, but the cereal campaign offers a different look at how that commercial profile can be connected to her foundation’s work.The campaign was not simply a personal $100,000 donation from Clark. The more than $100,000 figure represents money raised through Caitlin's Crunch Time campaign, while Hy-Vee provided the retail platform and pledged proceeds to the foundation.That distinction is important because Clark’s community work often involves partnerships that turn her popularity into support for youth programmes. Her foundation says its goal is to create opportunities for children to learn, grow and thrive through education, nutrition and sports.In Clarks’ case, the cereal became more than a piece of merchandise. articles.title: Asian Games: Just 700gm between Suchika Tariyal and spot in MMA final
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Nagoya: Suchika Tariyal did not lose her fight in the arena. She lost it on the weighing scale.In a dramatic finish to the traditional 60kg MMA semifi.
articles.body: Nagoya: Suchika Tariyal did not lose her fight in the arena. She lost it on the weighing scale.In a dramatic finish to the traditional 60kg MMA semifinal, the 36-year-old Indian was tied with Singapore’s Hui Hoon Toon after the bout and the mandatory one-minute extra time. Two judges voted for the Singaporean, while one sided with Suchika.Unhappy with the verdict, Suchika and her team felt she had landed more punches and strikes. The Mixed Martial Arts Sports Federation of India president Nikhil Kunder then lodged a protest with the Asian federation, sending the contest into arbitration.Asian Games Full Coverage |Schedule | Medal Tally“We had to pay a fee of $1,000 for the arbitration process. We get to choose three random judges, who go into a closed room and analyse the last round. They give their scores and, based on that, a decision is made. Even then, the match ended in a draw,” Kunder told TOI.The Singapore federation was then given two options: go for counter-arbitration, allowing them to choose three judges from the panel, or have the fighters weighed, with the lighter athlete at the morning weigh-in declared the winner.“They opted for the latter,” Kunder said.That left Suchika at a disadvantage. She was found to be 700gm heavier than her Singaporean opponent at the morning weigh-in and, under the sport’s Asian body rules, was eliminated from the final.Kunder said the Indian team was also unable to verify the weight themselves because the athletes were staying on the cruise ship.“The players are staying on the cruise ship, so we officials don’t have access to them. We didn’t get to see the weight and had to take what was told to us at face value,” he said.The decision left Suchika heartbroken.“She just wouldn’t stop crying. It was very difficult to console her. But we had to accept the situation,” Kunder said.Later, Suchika said, “I gave my 100%, and I don’t agree with the decision that went in her favour.”The medal was India’s first in the sport, which made its debut at this edition of the Games.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Himanshu Dhillon is a diehard Sunny Deol fan. His father, Shamsher Dhillon, has a doctorate in agriculture. The shooter’s motivational mantra, then, paraphrases a famous dialogue of his idol, his father’s profession and the farming he tried during the pandemic.“Yeh kisaan ka haath hai. Yeh lohe ko pighla kar uska aakaar badal deta hai (This is the hand of a farmer. He melts iron and shapes it).”Asian Games Full Coverage| Schedule| Medal TallyOn Monday, Dhillon didn’t melt metal; instead, he shot two of them, both silver, in the 10m air rifle at the Aichi Prefecture Shooting Range.First, the Asian Games debutant teamed up with Rudrankksh Patil and Parth Mane to clinch the men’s team silver. He returned later in the afternoon and, in a pulsating display of composure, concentration and precision, finished second (252.4) in the individual event, opening his individual tally at the senior international level.Patil, who at one stage held a 1.5-point lead, faltered and settled for bronze (230.9).It took a Games record by the reigning Olympic and Asian Games champion Lihao Sheng (254.2) to climb to the top of the podium. The Chinese shooter bettered his mark of 253.3 from the previous Games.Dhillon’s father sends him motivational messages daily. On the day, first came his 21st birthday wishes, followed by a message which read: “Whatever happens, you need to add a medal for India. The colour of the medal depends on you.”The message, in his native tongue, seemed to strike a chord. While Patil hit the front, Sheng and Dhillon played catch-up. A 10.2 and 9.7 relegated Patil. Dhillon was also pegged back by a 9.8, which gave the Chinese the unassailable lead, but his three 10.9s did the trick.It was a contest of fine margins, with four 10.9s in an elimination series and three shoot-offs deciding positions.From wrestling to shootingDhillon’s journey is only beginning, but the junior World Cup gold medallist already has an eye on the legacy he would like. In shooting, he idolises Abhinav Bindra. His sporting hero, though, is Virat Kohli.“I’m very inspired by Virat Kohli,” he said.As he walked away with two silver medals around his neck, the significance of the day was not lost on him.“This is the best birthday gift I could have given myself,” he said.But he did not begin as a shooter. Inspired by his uncle Hardeep Singh Dhillon, who represented India in Greco-Roman wrestling at the 2016 Rio Olympics, his father enrolled him in an akhada. It took just two weeks to realise wrestling was not for him.“I found wrestling a bit hard, so I later opted for shooting while studying in a Gurukul in Kudri,” he said with a laugh.Once he found his calling at the range, his family backed him despite financial constraints.“My parents left our village for me. It’s their sacrifices that have got me here,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chess Olympiad Round 6: How Nihal Sarin blundered his queen, and India suffered heartbreaking loss to Uzbekistan
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: On Monday, India's open team was paired against hot favourites and tournament hosts Uzbekistan in Round 6 of the 46th Chess Olympiad in Sam.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: On Monday, India's open team was paired against hot favourites and tournament hosts Uzbekistan in Round 6 of the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand.The anticipation around this fixture had been building since before the tournament began, perhaps because these two nations have won the last two Olympiads between them, or because Dommaraju Gukesh will face Javokhir Sindarov for the World Championship later this year, or simply because these are, right now, two of the most potent chess nations on the planet.India had arrived at the board sitting in the leading group after five rounds, level with Uzbekistan and Germany at the top of the standings, which only added to the stakes. Hence, captain Srinath Narayanan put the strongest line-up forward, with Praggnanandhaa on Board 1, Arjun Erigaisi on 2, Nihal Sarin on 3, and Gukesh on 4.Consequently, Vidit Gujrathi had a rest day, thanks to which he was momentarily part of the ChessBase India commentary team at the venue.His eyes lit up when Nodirbek Yakubboev, playing White, pushed 35.f4 against Nihal. With every other board on the day ending in or heading towards a draw, this was the one game left with a winner in it.Nihal replied 35...e3, and Vidit's eyes only became brighter. Yakubboev's 36.fxg5+ put India in a genuinely promising position.But then what followed was a sequence no Indian fan would have wanted to see — 36...Kxg5 37.g3 Nf5.Vidit felt Nihal, sensing a clear advantage, got swept up in the moment and pushed a little too hard. Soon after, his queen was captured (40.Qxc7), and the entire commentary panel, Vidit included, could only put their hands on their heads.The disappointment was more palpable because Nihal still had plenty of time left on the clock. This wasn't a case of time pressure forcing a mistake, just a hanging piece missed in the heat of a winning position. But that is what it was.Amid all that activity, Nihal's queen was left completely undefended on c7. Yakubboev's 40.Qxc7 simply took it for free.From a position where Black had real winning chances just a few moves earlier, the game swung entirely in White's favour, and Yakubboev converted the resulting material advantage into a full point without much further resistance.It proved decisive. With Praggnanandhaa, Erigaisi and Gukesh all drawing their games on the other three boards, Nihal's loss was the difference. Uzbekistan won the match 2.5-1.5, handing India their first team defeat of the tournament in the open section.India's women back to winning ways India's women, by contrast, had a comfortable day at the office after a Round 5 defeat to Poland, beating the United States 3-1 on Monday.Koneru Humpy and Divya Deshmukh both drew their games against higher-pedigree opposition in Carissa Yip and Alice Lee, but the difference came further down the order, with Vantika Agrawal beating the experienced Irina Krush, and Savitha Shri getting the better of Rose Atwell.Tuesday is the tournament's only scheduled rest day, a timely break for India's open side after a result that will sting more for how close it came to going the other way than for the actual damage on the scoreboard.Play resumes on Wednesday with Round 7, when India's open team takes on England, and the women's team faces Germany.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 49ers head coach details plan for overcoming WR injuries
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers will look to their own roster as part of their search for wide receiver help following Demarcus Robinson's injury.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers need wide receiver help after veteran Demarcus Robinson went down with an injury in Week 2. He's the third of the 49ers top four projected WRs to get hurt so far this season, but that doesn't necessarily mean the 49ers will look outside the building for help.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan on Sunday indicated the team would look for some additional help outside the building. There are a handful of veteran options available and if the 49ers sign someone it'll likely be to their practice squad. Shanahan on Monday said the team will lean on internal options to fill the void left by Robinson on game days.

"No, we expect those guys to be up and everyone's got to get more involved," Shanahan said. "But, I know our guys, John [Lynch] and his group, are working on all possibilities, looking at everything that's out there and our options here for this week and going forward."

The 49ers have two WRs on their 53-man roster who haven't played much this season. Jacob Cowing saw 24 offensive snaps in Week 2 after Robinson's injury. Second-year player Jordan Watkins has been a healthy scratch in the first two games. That duo should get some additional opportunities.

Veteran KhaDarel Hodge also had more chances with Robinson out, and he turned in his first catch of the year Sunday. Shanahan said he'll be among the players the 49ers will lean on, but it's not going to be a one-person effort.

"Yes. He's been out there the last couple weeks," Shanahan said. "He had a catch yesterday later in the game and he made some key blocks versus the Rams. Pretty much all our guys who are up, we always mix them in on offense, but as you lose starters and stuff, those guys have to be able to do more and more."

It sounds like the 49ers won't try to directly replace Robinson, but instead rely on the various skill sets of their other pass catchers to try and recreate his production in the aggregate. San Francisco may also turn more heavily toward WR Mike Evans and tight end George Kittle . Kittle caught four balls for 80 yards and a touchdown after Robinson went out Sunday. Evans has been good, but he only had 10 targets in the first two games, including three in Week 2. Additional production from those veterans should also play a role in the 49ers figuring out their WR position until internal reinforcements come.

Christian Kirk is eligible to come off IR in Week 5, and Robinson is only expected to miss three-to-six weeks. De'Zhaun Stribling is also on track to return late in the season.

The 49ers will likely wind up adding another veteran pass catcher to their practice squad for internal depth. For now it sounds like the plan is to rely on players on their 53-man roster first before they start turning to new additions to the receiving corps.

articles.title: Dallas Stars top 3: DeSmith kicks, Rantanen floats, & everybody fights in preseason win vs Blues
articles.summary: The Dallas Stars swept the home-and-home with a 2-1 preseason win against the St. Louis Blues at American Airlines Center on Monday. Stars lines Shoot the pu...
articles.body:
The Dallas Stars swept the home-and-home with a 2-1 preseason win against the St. Louis Blues at American Airlines Center on Monday.

Last season, Dallas had trouble shooting the puck. Like, at all. They were often double digits behind the opponent in shot count, and even though that is far from everything in a game, the difference was often apparent in the way the game was played.

The Stars have been pretty transparent with their approach to creating more offense this season. They want to maintain the defensive habits this organization has had for years, while adding a bit more speed and creativity up the ice. Shooting the puck will also be a part of that, but don't expect them to turn into Carolina and abandon their goal of holding onto pucks.

Tonight, in preseason game two, we have seen a few examples of quick ups by the defensemen. As Thomas Harley said the other day, quick and controlled breakout passes should theoretically allow the Stars to play with speed while also maintaining possession of the puck. Rather than skating behind the net and waiting for the rest of the guys to change, defensemen pick their heads up and decide whether there is an easy play ahead of them.

That has nothing to do with the Stars first goal of the game, though. But it did come because Harley found some open space and shot the puck. This shot looked to be on the ice but then went in over Joel Hofer 's pad, so maybe it hit a skate on the way.

This is one of the reasons I think Harley should QB PP1. But hey, what do I know?

Outside of the goal, there was another fight. Jack Anderson fought for what I believe is the third time between preseason and the prospect tournament. And he fought Dylan Peterson, who also fought on Saturday in St. Louis.

Casey DeSmith was excellent, as Dallas got into a bit too much circling in its own end and not enough stopping on pucks. DeSmith has one of the quickest pad flash saves I have seen in the NHL. He's great at that when plays break down.

The Stars have made it a nice habit of fighting a million times this preseason. I dig it.

Tonight, the second tilt was once again Kyle Burroughs , who was once again pushed into a fight in defense after he committed a penalty. And Burroughs got the better of Dylan Holloway (a scorer, not a fighter), switching to his left hand and throwing a perfect straight down the middle that dropped Holloway. Holloway went to the room and did not return.

After that fight, Dallas decided to take 100 penalties and went down 5-on-3 for at least two full minutes, with some 5v4 mixed in. Somehow, thanks very much to Trey Taylor's shot blocking, the Stars made it through every kill and went into the third period still up 1-0.

The penalties did not result in a goal, but they did result in this hilarity:

While they obviously won't fight this much during the season, I do love the don't-take-s**t attitude this team has adopted under Glen Gulutzan.

It's a small shift, but they don't sit back and take it anymore. When a teammate is hit, or there is a cheap shot, another player is right there in Victory Green to drop the gloves or put them in a headlock. I would've loved to see this attitude when they had the deep team they had both years against Edmonton in the WCF.

As a hockey player, nothing much beats the feeling of being able to walk into a puck just sitting there for you and hammer it as hard as you can. Like the hardest shot All-Star competition, it just feels freeing. Especially if you can hammer it at over 100 mph. I cannot.

But tonight, Nils Lundkvist had that opportunity, and he sort of made it count.

After a nice setup from Dylan Hryckowian to Mikko Rantanen, Rantanen tossed a backhand back into the slot for Lundkvist to skate into. It looked to me like Lundkvist hammered the one-timer and burnt a hole through the chest of the Blues netminder. But when asked about it, Lundkvist called it a muffin shot, saying he actually didn't get much of it.

So maybe it actually fooled the goalie instead?

St. Louis scored on a quirky bounce in tight to make it 2-1 and scare all of us that we would see one of the worst things in sports: preseason overtime. But DeSmith and the Stars held on and improved to 2-0 in the preseason, sweeping the Blues in the home-and-home.

Later in the third period, Jason Robertson gave the entire AAC a chuckle when he did his best wacky waving inflatable arm flailing tube man impression while defending a 2-on-1.

Yes, Jason Robertson defending a 2-on-1. It was as glorious as it sounds. And it worked.

Stars coach Glen Gulutzan on Casey DeSmith

"Same old Casey. Bottom line is he's competitive… He's a competitive guy in practice, he's a competitive guy in games. He's vocal in the locker room… he's earned that."

I thought Dylan Hryckowian was great tonight. He was all over the ice, had a few great chances on what is a very quick-release snapshot, and he was in the scrums along with his brother.

I dare you to go back and watch Mikko Rantanen's shifts from this game. Actually, I don't even know if that is possible to do, but it would be very funny. Rantanen played tonight like he was in a roller hockey game on Huntington Beach. He kind of floated around, tried a dangle here, tossed a puck chest-high there, and stickhandled his way through just about any Blues skater that came his way. It was funny and impressive.

Arno Tiefensee was hurt at morning skate and did not dress tonight, as Brandon Halverson took his spot as backup. We should know more tomorrow about his status.

Colin Blackwell is not expected to miss much time, likely just days, after being helped off the ice during camp last week.

Matt Duchene has still not skated at camp for an unknown "maintenance" reason, but is expected to skate this week.

Cameron Hughes left the game 22 seconds in after taking a hit. He was seen in a sling after the game and is dealing with an upper-body injury that we should know more about tomorrow.

Trey Taylor played over two minutes on one extended PK and blocked 2-3 shots. He was great tonight and is right on the edge of being an NHL defenseman.
