articles.title: Colts Add 22-Touchdown Weapon Amid Recent Alec Pierce News
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts added a wide receiver to the roster after Alec Pierce's ankle injury that will sideline him The post Colts Add 22-Touchdown Weapon Ami...
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts will be without wide receiver Alec Pierce due to an aggravated ankle injury that will force him out for "several weeks."

A recent update reveals that instead of surgery, the wide receiver will get therapy. Ian Rapoport mentions that Pierce could return sometime in the middle of the season if everything goes well.

Needing help in the receiver room, the Colts have signed a seven-season veteran to the squad.

According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Colts are signing Darius Slayton .

"Sources: The #Colts are signing former #Giants WR Darius Slayton. Slayton compiled 296 catches for 4,435 yards and 22 TDs during his seven-year tenure in New York."

Josh Downs and Keenan Allen are the current top options for Indianapolis. But the addition of Slayton will give the team depth with Pierce out for the time being.

Now in Indy, Darius Slayton will reunite with a former long-time teammate.

Darius Slayton Reunites with Quarterback

With Darius Slayton headed to Indianapolis, the wide receiver will play with former New York Giants teammate Daniel Jones .

Both selected in the 2019 NFL Draft, the pair played six seasons together while on the Giants and proved to be a strong duo. Slayton logged his best receiving yardage and best touchdown season with Jones throwing his way.

Back in 2023, Slayton revealed that he would like to play with Jones for the rest of his career.

"I consider myself blessed, because there have been hundreds of thousands of receivers that have come into this league and had a veteran quarterback or a rough quarterback situation. Getting to grow alongside the franchise guy is a very blessed position to be in," Slayton said, via The Athletic . "I'm just fortunate I'm here. I'm fortunate I was drafted alongside of him, and I look forward to working with him."

Now reunited with the AFC South team, the pair can get back to work and help the Colts snap an eight-game losing streak that began in the 2025 season.

Before Slayton signed with the Colts, Insider Josina Anderson noted Indy could be an option due to his history with Jones. Now, two weeks later, the former 2019 draftees are playing together once more.

As noted above, the Indianapolis Colts are on a nine-game losing streak and were close to snapping that in the Week 2 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs .

The offense has thrown for less than 400 yards through two games and with injuries preventing them from performing at their best, it will be hard to snap that streak.

The addition of Darius Slayton to the roster, who has chemistry with Daniel Jones , could help the team's offensive woes.

Indianapolis currently has the longest losing streak in the NFL and aims to get its first win of the season against the Houston Texans , who also started the season with two losses.

If the team doesn't get back on track, it could spell the end of the Shane Steichen era.

articles.title: TJ Friedl’s 5 Best Moments as a Cincinnati Red After DFA
articles.summary: From game-saving robberies to his first career homer against the Dodgers, relive the gritty defensive gems and clutch hits that defined a fan favorite’s six-...
articles.body:
Former Cincinnati Reds outfielder TJ Friedl was designated for assignment Sunday afternoon, ending his six-year stint with the club that took a nosedive in the 2026 season. The Reds claimed infielder Oswaldo Cabrera off waivers from the New York Yankees .

In 91 games, Friedl hit .172 with a .510 OPS. He had 41 total hits and just 11 extra-base hits, rendering him basically a non-factor offensively. He had multiple stints in Triple-A with the Louisville Bats, bouncing back and forth as the Reds struggled with outfield injuries.

However, that wasn't always the case. From 2022-2025, Friedl was essentially Cincinnati's everyday center fielder, providing a contact-hitting, scrappy offensive player while playing a great brand of defense in center field.

Let's go through some of the best moments of Friedl's career in a Reds uniform.

Home run robbery to beat the Milwaukee Brewers

Teams don't often walk off a game with a great defensive play, but that's what happened in 2025 for TJ Friedl. With a runner on base, Emilio Pagan allowed a hard-hit, deep line drive to lefty Jake Bauers , but Friedl timed a jump to rob Bauers and end the game, shocking everyone but Pagan.

First career home run/ Mookie Betts favor

Friedl hit his first career home run against the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2021, sending it about 10 rows deep into the right-field seats. Los Angeles outfielder Mookie Betts got the ball out of the stands for Friedl and, in return, gave the fan a signed bat.

The power-hitting Laureano got a hold of one off lefty Andrew Abbott to deep center field. Friedl was playing rather in and had to run a long way and track it perfectly, catching a ball that was clearly going to be a home run. Given the circumstances, the catch against the Brewers was the bigger play, but this one was the better overall defensive play.

Walk-off single over Texas Rangers in 2023

The first of two walk-offs in a series in which the Reds swept the Rangers, Jonathan India walked and advanced to second on a passed ball. Will Smith then threw an up-and-away fastball, which Friedl pulled into the right-center field gap, scoring India and winning the game.

Diving catch against Rafael Devers in August 2026

Despite a horrible season, Friedl still put his body on the line for the Reds. Rafael Devers hit a line drive into center field, and Friedl went full extension to make the grab and rob Devers of a hit.

articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams shared noteworthy news on star wide receiver Davante Adams during their game against the New York Giants. The post LA Rams Announce Dava...

With Puka Nacua sidelined, the Los Angeles Rams passing attack rested largely in the capable hands of Davante Adams , and he delivered. Adams tallied 118 yards and 1 touchdown on four receptions less than 20 minutes (game time) into the action.

His efforts helped him move up the historical rankings.

"With 118 receiving yards tonight and counting, Davante Adams has passed Art Monk (12,721) to enter the top 25 on the NFL's all-time receiving yards list," Rams PR posted during the game.

The Rams scored a second touchdown on a Stafford pass to running back Kyren Williams . But that was also set up by Adams, who hauled in a 64-yarder, which is what triggered the announcement from the Rams.

Davante Adams Called Rams' Offensive Explosion

Adams was among those atteempting to quell the concerns about the Rams following their 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1.

"Everybody's freaking out, which I understand. We didn't put to together the greatest showing out there. But at the end of the day, you're a fool if you think that that's what it's going to look like every single week. At the end of the day, there were a few different variables that we shouldn't have to deal with moving forward. And one of them being the first week, which is part of it. And then, obviously, traveling," Adams told reporters on September 17.

"We're not making excuses, but that is a potential reason why we, maybe, weren't as energetic or–but at the end of the day the execution is the execution. Once you get a man in front of you, I'm not falling asleep as he's you know standing there in front of me. So, you still got to go and block him and um go run good routes and get open. So, at the end of the day, we got our minds right to to do the right thing. And like I say, the way we practice, the way we get each other ready, it gives us the best shot at being ready on … Monday."

articles.title: Ceiling, floor, expectations: Mitchell Robinson with the Boston Celtics in 2026-27
articles.summary: Let's dive into our assessment for Mitchell Robinson for this edition of our player projections for the campaign soon to arrive.
articles.body:
As each day of the 2026 NBA offseason passes, we inch closer to the start of the 2026-27 regular season for the Boston Celtics . And as Opening Night draws nearer, the outline of the roster that will take the floor for Game 1 of 82 is starting to come into focus as well.

After Celtics President of Basketball Operations Brad Stevens traded star forward Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers , it became clear that this is a critical season for the team's current contention arc, with the team being remade to maximize the rest of the team's sole superstar, Jayson Tatum . What is the ceiling, floor, and our expectation for each of the players currently under contract with Boston given this sea change in structure for the team?

To such an end, Daniel Donabedian and Justin Quinn of the Celtics Wire took a player-by-player deep dive into the answers for these questions. So let's dive into our assessment for Mitchell Robinson for this edition of our player projections for the campaign soon to arrive.

JQ : The ceiling for Robinson is a healthier, more available version of himself that takes the floor somewhere north of 65 games, something that has happened only twice in the eight seasons the Western Kentucky alum has managed over the course of an eight-season career in the league.

That outcome isn't a wild one given Boston's big man depth and the Celtics proven capabilities of helping keep aging and injury-prone players reasonably healthy over the course of an 82-game season. It probably means he plays under 20 minutes a game (maybe even closer to 15) throughout the regular season with a small ramp-up at the end of the campaign.

DD : The Celtics trading Jaylen Brown dominated headlines, but adding center Mitchell Robinson was arguably the Green Team's second-biggest move of the offseason. The reigning NBA champion provides Boston with a formidable shot-blocker who knows the ins-and-outs of his former team: the rival New York Knicks .

If he can stay healthy, Robinson could transform the Celtics' defense while locking down the paint. His ability to crash the boards should make him a quick favorite of head coach Joe Mazzulla as well, guaranteeing the 7-footer a spot in the big man rotation — and maybe even the starting lineup. Regardless of whether or not he starts, Robinson has the potential to make the C's one of the best rebounding teams in the league next season.

JQ : Injuries have eaten tree-quarters and then some of Robinson's season just the year before last, and that, more or less, would be the crux of any worst-case outcome for the Louisiana native with Boston. His player type is not all that different from that of Neemias Queta , meaning integrating him into the team's play style ought not to be a major concern.

And his personality is laid back and focused on winning, the 7-foot big man known for his affable nature and team-first approach to professionalism. So any analysis of what might go wrong here starts and ends with his availability to play based on health.

DD : Robinson's floor is pretty simple. The 28-year-old won't be worth the annual $15 million the Celtics are paying him if he misses over half of the regular season. His fit with this roster is apparent, yet so is his injury risk, as Robinson hasn't played in more than 60 games in a single regular season since the 2021-22 campaign.

We know what Robinson can do at his best. He's an NBA champion who can serve as the centerpiece of a top-tier defense. The first-year Celtic just needs a relatively clean bill of health to make all of that possible. If Robinson can't stay healthy, he won't take the starting job from center Neemias Queta and Boston will have to get creative at the five spot.

JQ :I expect Robinson to suit up for 55-60 contests with the Celtics this season, resting on back-to-backs and in busier stretches to help keep him health for the postseason. His role will be similar as to what he played with the New York Knicks , and his counting stats should largely stay the same as they have throughout his career.

Keep an eye on his free throws given Boston's capabilities in developing players even once they enter their prime on smaller aspects of their game, with a number of Boston alumni seeing their efficiency at the charity stripe improve after some time with the team.

DD : Despite the fact that Robinson has played for the Knicks his entire career, I think he'll gel well with the Celtics (and Mazzulla, especially). He brings the offensive rebounding prowess they're looking for and could give Boston a terrific one-two punch at center alongside Queta.

For now, I predict that he'll come off the bench to begin the season and start in certain spots when the C's expect their opponents to abuse a Hack-a-Robinson strategy. I don't know how much he'll burn foes for that at the line, however, I do picture him bolstering Boston's defense and becoming a Robert Williams-like Celtic — if healthy.

articles.title: Five Burning Questions Surrounding Michigan Football Ahead Of Iowa Game
articles.summary: Michigan is 3-0 and back in the top 25 after some ups and downs and because of the rollercoaster ride, there are plenty of questions surrounding the Wolverin...
articles.body:
With Michigan coming off a 52-16 win over UTEP and heading into a top-20 matchup with Iowa to open Big Ten play, there are a lot of legitimate questions beyond "can Michigan win?"

Michigan's starting quarterback has been under incredible scrutiny to start the 2026 season but he's gotten better week after week. He turned into a major ball carrier against Oklahoma and was a big part of that upset win. Against UTEP, he played his best game going 19-of-25 for 223 yards and two touchdowns. He also had 22 yards on the ground. He did lose another fumble, which he needs to clean up, but he was solid all around.

Underwood needs to take another step forward against an incredibly disciplined and opportunistic Iowa defense. If he keeps improving week after week, he's going to put Michigan in a position to win a lot of games.

Michigan only averaged 4.4 yards per carry against UTEP, which is not going to be good enough against a defense like Iowa. Jordan Marshall is a little dinged up, so it'll be interesting to see who is even available on Saturday. Luckily for Michigan, freshman Savion Hiter and Bryson Kuzdzal can easily step up in Marshall's absence.

Iowa's defense is stout and currently No. 11 in the country against the run. If Michigan can't be somewhat productive on the ground against the Hawkeyes , it's going to be a tough day for the offense.

Michigan didn't score a point in the first quarter against UTEP and found itself down 7-0 after the first 15 minutes. That cannot happen against a fundamentally sound football team like Iowa. If you fall behind the Hawkeyes, you might not ever get back in front of them. They're too good on defense and Kirk Ferentz knows how to keep another team's offense on the sidelines. Michigan has to score early and often to put the pressure on Iowa's offense.

Iowa is in the top 25 when it comes to turnover margin, while Michigan is outside of the top 100 . That formula will not work when a Kirk Ferentz team comes to town. The Hawkeyes don't make mistakes and don't beat themselves. If Michigan gets loose with the ball and loses a couple of fumbles (again) or if Underwood throws it to the wrong team, things could go sideways for the Wolverines in a hurry.

This is obviously a big picture question, but it's Kyle Whittingham's first chance to win a game in conference . He got a big one a couple of weeks ago against Oklahoma, who was ranked No. 11 at the time, and he's currently undefeated as Michigan's head man. If he can get another W against Iowa to start off 1-0 in the Big Ten, it'll just add another shot of confidence for him, his staff and his players as they dig deeper into conference play.

articles.title: Rams news: Matthew Stafford connects with Terrance Ferguson for 4th TD vs. Giants
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams took the New York Giants to task on Monday night. Naturally, Matthew Stafford led the charge. He had Davante Adams at his side putting...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams took the New York Giants to task on Monday night. Naturally, Matthew Stafford led the charge .

He had Davante Adams at his side putting up the points , and rookie TE Terrance Ferguson . At the 9:02 mark of the 4th quarter, Stafford found Ferguson with ease to convert on a touchdown at 2nd-and-goal. This put the Rams up 28-6 and, as a result, snatched their first win of the season.

In total, Stafford had completed 22 out of 31 pass attempts for 327 yards and 4 touchdowns. The Rams also avenged a 27-6 season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers .

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

In the process, Stafford surpassed Phillip Rivers on the all-time touchdown list to be in 6th place. Now he trails Tom Brady , Brett Favre, Peyton Manning , Aaron Rodgers , and Drew Brees .

Throughout 18 seasons in the NFL, Stafford has established himself as one of the most decorated QBs of his time. He holds the record for being the fastest player to reach 40,000 career passing yards. In 2022, he led the Rams to a Super Bowl victory over the Cincinatti Bengals. Two years later, Stafford won his first career NFL MVP Award , edging out Drake Maye of the Patriots by one point.

Going into this season, the Rams are poised to be one of the league's elite teams. A main reason for that is the return of Aaron Donald after his retirement. Donald, alongside Stafford and Myles Garrett , makes the Rams a perennial Super Bowl contender on paper.

Stafford's retirement isn't on the horizon yet. A Super Bowl win would be the best way to cap it all off.

articles.title: Pave Ruth
articles.summary: "Yesterday's home runs don't win today's games"
articles.body:
A gut punching series loss at the hands of the Miami Marlins not only had the Diamondbacks lose more ground in the NL Wild Card race to the 3 teams ahead of them, it also seemed to take all the hopium that remained in our systems and replace it with either copium or just straight up despair as the D'Backs would go from 2 losing series against 2 sub .500 teams to welcoming the New York Yankees into town for the final home series of the 2026 season.

The Yankees may have already secured their spot in October before their trip to the desert but with a chance at the AL East title still a possibility, along with having Gerrit Cole and the probable AL Cy Young winner in Cam Schlittler taking the bump, this would be no cake walk of a series and the Diamondbacks would need to at least win this series if they want any sliver of hope going into their final 6 games in Colorado and San Diego . With the 25th anniversary of the 2001 World Series winning team being celebrated this series, maybe they would be able to have some of that magic rub off onto this 2026 ballclub and use it as the fuel they need to propel them towards postseason baseball.

Eduardo Rodriguez has undoubtedly been the best starter in the Diamondbacks rotation for all of 2026 as he leads the starters in wins (15), ERA (2.89), IP (183.2) and K's (140), but the issue that has been rearing its head all season for Rodriguez has been his struggles out of the gate and we got more of the same in Friday night's series opener with the Yankees putting up a 5 spot before the Diamondbacks even had the chance to swing the lumber.

The three of us looked at ERod's numbers from the 1st inning of his starts compared to the rest of the game and it was as night and day as it could get with his first inning ERA this season sitting at 7.84, a WHIP of 1.77 and an opposing slash of .302/.389/579. From the 2nd inning and beyond he evolves into a completely different pitcher with his 1.89 ERA, 1.12 WHIP and opposing hitter slashing just .222/.279/.326. This isn't even necessarily just an issue he's had in 2026 either as his career ERA in the 1st inning (4.51) compared to the rest of his innings (3.92) shows that he's always had struggles early in games for most of his career.

With the demoralizing 9-2 loss on Friday night the Diamondbacks and all snakes fans in attendance would hope that the vibes would be turned around as Saturday would be the big 25th anniversary celebration of the greatest world series of all time (yes I'm biased) with so many legends from that squad like Randy Johnson, Luis Gonzalez, Tony Womack, Miguel Batista, Damien Miller and more in the building for the festivities.

Both the Yankees and Diamondbacks had clutch pitching and hitting at times throughout this game as the score was knotted at 3 a piece going into the bottom of the 9th inning with the Snakes in desperate need of a win to keep their playoff hopes from lowering even further, and that's when the infamous Pavin Smith stepped in the box as a pinch hitter with a runner on 1st and 1 out. The baseball gods must like reruns because they decided that a Diamondbacks walk-off of the Yankees on the night of the 2001 WS celebration would be the most fitting outcome, and Pavin delivered just that with a 2-R home run into the sea of Yankee fans in right field.

All 3 of us have been very vocal in our frustrations with Smith's struggles in his career here in the desert and the front office seeming to refuse to move on from a player that has accumulated 0.1 bWAR in his time as a major leaguer, and we all still feel that he should not be on this roster at the beginning of the 2027 season (if we have one that is) in any capacity, but we did admit that it was nice to see Pavin summon his inner Luis Gonzalez and send the fans into a frenzy with a walk-off over the Yankees.

The fireworks might have been after the game on Friday night, but Sunday's final home game of the 2026 regular season had plenty of leftovers as it felt like baseballs were flying out left and right. Most of them came for the Yankees off of Corbin Burnes in the 4th inning, but the biggest one was in the Diamondbacks favor with Nolan Arenado hitting a go ahead (and potential season saving) grand slam in the 5th inning, his 3rd in 2026 and the 9th of his career.

The fellas and I discussed how nice of a surprise this offensive resurgence has been from Arenado as he is putting up some of the best numbers at the dish we have seen since his MVP caliber season as a Cardinal in 2022 while also pondering the likelihood that Nolan can get to 30 home runs on the season (27 currently) with 3 of the final 6 games being played in his old stomping grounds of Coors Field where Arenado has 139 dingers in his career in the mile high city.

Setting off for the final road trip of the regular season the Snakes will be heading to Coors Field to take on the Colorado Rockies as they continue to battle for their lives in an attempt to make miracles happen and sneak into the playoffs.

The last few weeks have seen us and other fans throw the term "must-win games" around a bunch but these 3 in Colorado are all truly must win games if the Diamondbacks want to have any real chance at making the final series in San Diego mean anything as a Diamondbacks loss+Padres win, 2 D'Backs losses or 2 Padres wins would put the final nail in the coffin of the Diamondbacks playoff hopes.

Gabe, Brandon and I all felt disgusted that we would have to actually root for the Los Angeles Dodgers to win baseball games (just typing that out makes me want to puke) but that is the reality we are in as a Dodgers sweep of the Padres with the Diamondbacks sweeping the Rockies would set us up for what could most likely feel like its own wild card series against the Padres in San Diego to decide who gets in and who goes to Cancun.

articles.title: Former Commanders' starting TE heads back to Eagles
articles.summary: Former Commanders TE Zach Ertz is returning to his original NFL home.
articles.body:
Zach Ertz was one of Jayden Daniels ' favorite targets for the past two seasons with the Washington Commanders . However, last December, Ertz tore his ACL, and the Commanders did not re-sign him after the 2025 season. Ertz, who turns 36 in November, made it clear he planned to play in 2026 and didn't want his career to end on that note; he's back — but not with Washington.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reported on Monday that Ertz was signing with the Philadelphia Eagles ' practice squad. Ertz, who spent his first 8.5 seasons with the Eagles, provides depth at tight end with starter Dallas Goedert dealing with a sprained MCL.

During his two seasons with the Commanders, Ertz started 30 games, caught 116 passes for 1,158 yards and 11 touchdowns. He was a key part of Washington's 2024 playoff run, too.

Over his 13-year NFL career, Ertz has caught 825 passes for 8,592 receiving yards and 57 touchdowns. Ertz was a part of the Eagles' first-ever Super Bowl victory in 2017, including catching the go-ahead touchdown pass in the win over the New England Patriots.

Washington signed tight end Chig Okonkwo to a three-year deal in March to be its No. 1 tight end. The Commanders also have John Bates , Ben Sinnott and Colson Yankoff . The Commanders and Eagles faced off in Week 1 and will meet again in Week 8.

articles.title: Four down territory: Takeaways from Rams first win of season
articles.summary: Aaron Donald’s first game back is biggest takeaway from Monday Night Football
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are in the win column for the 2026 season thanks to a 28-6 victory over the New York Giants . The Rams controlled the majority of the game after Jaxson Dart exited early because of an MCL sprain suffered in the first quarter. But the major news belonged to Aaron Donald and Co., as the legendary defensive tackle played his first game for the Rams after spending two years in retirement. Here are the 4 biggest takeaways from Monday Night's win for LA; starting with the future Hall of Famer…

The juice that came from SoFi Stadium when Aaron Donald was announced out of the tunnel was unlike any other.

Aaron Donald may not have registered a sack in the game but his impact was felt. The energy of the Rams defense was the best it has been since its win against the Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football last year… which coincidentally was "Aaron Donald Night". AD only played 58% of the snaps and it was a reasonable snap count for the legendary player.

The Rams defensive line is going to be fresh all season long now because of Aaron Donald's insertion into the lineup. Kobie Turner was a menace early and Braden Fiske did damage late in the game. This does not even include the effect that Myles Garrett may have when he returns.

This unit will be the best in football in due time.

In my opinion, if you watch the tape, there is no debate who should be the Rams starting running back. Blake Corum is the more explosive runner in my opinion. He hits the hole with conviction whereas Kyren Williams dances just a hair too long. That indecisiveness has prevented the Rams from having the opportunity to break long runs. I think if given the opportunity, Corum could provide more explosion to the Rams offense.

Both running backs rushed 12 times against the Giants. Williams outrushed Corum 85 yards to 79 yards. Both fumbled, but Kyren Williams lost his fumble; leading to an easy Giants field goal. Had the Giants been more formidable, the turnover could have been costly (flashback to Week 5 vs. SF).

After the Puka Nacua injury news broke, I emphasized that the spotlight was on Adams to show up and earn his 2 year contract (for more than just a redzone touchdown magnet). Well, #17 must have heard loud and clear because he had his best game as a Ram; registering 8 receptions (10 targets) for 195 yards and 2 touchdowns. He made a bunch of highlight reel grabs throughout the first three quarters of the game. Hopefully, Puka Nacua returns soon but Adams at least showed that he still has game left in him and is a solid #2 in the passing game.

4th Down: Matthew Stafford 's Monday Night Performance

Entering the game tonight, Stafford had a 1-5 career record as a Ram in Monday Night Football games. He needed to deliver. And he sure did. Earlier this week, I had predicted 4 touchdown passes and #9 delivered with – you bet – 4 touchdowns.

With 7 primetime games on this year's schedule, Matthew Stafford is going to be in the spotlight a lot. The Rams need him to show up more like he did tonight than the Australia-type performance.

articles.title: Otters using old and new school methods prepping for a brand new opponent
articles.summary: EVANSVILLE, In. (WEHT) — Many things can change in a decade. Let’s look back at 2016. The first season of stranger things premiered on Netflix, apple release...
articles.body:
EVANSVILLE, In. (WEHT) -- Many things can change in a decade. Let's look back at 2016. The first season of stranger things premiered on Netflix, apple released the I-phone seven, and the Evansville Otters won the frontier league championship. A lot has changed since then. But there's a saying that goes the more things change the more they stay the same. Which is certainly what Otters fans are hoping as they try to win their first frontier league championship since 2016.

The Otters will be taking on the Ottawa Titans in a five-game series. First two at home then the rest on the road. Evansville rolled back into town today after beating the Washington Wild Things 9-6 in the winner take all game five of the conference championship. Field manager Andy McCauley says the team had the day off, but the staff is already prepping for the challenges the titans pose. The otters haven't played Ottawa all year, but McCauley says they won't be going in completely blind.

"Luckily my three assistant coaches with Billy Easley, TJ, Zarewicz, Max Peterson are very adept at, pulling from the Trackman data, the video clips that we got from you guys, as well as Home Team Network, to give us a scouting report of what we're facing. I've reached out to some of my buddies that that manage on the other side that did face Ottawa, and I get a verbal scouting report from them, and that's how we used to have to do it," said McCauley, "But, the new technology is the way of the world. I think we'll be prepared just from an analytical and video, replay standpoint. No one does it better than those three guys. So, I'm pretty confident we'll be prepared.

Game one of the series against the Titans is set for tomorrow at 6:35 p-m in historic Bosse Field.

articles.title: Brian Burns, Andrew Thomas injuries add to Giants’ misery
articles.summary: More injury woes for the Giants.
articles.body:
As if the New York Giants needed more bad news on Monday night, star players Brian Burns and Andrew Thomas suffered injuries late in the Giants' lopsided 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.

Thomas, the team's left tackle, suffered a groin injury.

Burns was helped off the field with what appeared to be a left ankle injury. Per John Harbaugh after the game, Burns has a low ankle sprain.

Jordan Raanan of ESPN reports that Burns was wearing a boot and being driven to the team bus on a golf cart.

The good news is that Burns was able to leave the field under his own power, which demonstrates that his ankle was stable enough to walk on and bear his weight. That suggests either a Grade 1 or Grade 2 sprain, per Harvard Health . A Grade 1 low ankle sprain has a recovery time of 1 to 3 weeks, while a Grade 2 sprain has a recovery time of 3-6 weeks.

Typically treatment for a low ankle sprain involves a RICE (Rice, Ice, Compression, Elevation) regimen, resting the ankle as much as possible for the first 24 to 48 hours, and icing regularly. Given that the Giants need to travel from Los Angeles to New Jersey, the use of a boot isn't much of a surprise and shouldn't be particularly alarming at this point. As with Jaxson Dart , we'll get more information on his prognosis as the week unfolds.

Thomas has had an injury-plagued career, but has been healthy all spring and summer until now. Burns is coming off a career-best season. He was seen at the end of the game on the bench with a wrap on his left ankle.

The Giants also had an injury scare with wide receiver Malik Nabers in the second quarter, but he returned to action after having his shoulder checked.

These are all cornerstone players for the Giants that they cannot afford to be without.

We will get more information on all of the injuries, especially Dart's, as soon as it becomes available.

articles.title: 4 things we learned from the Giants’ 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams
articles.summary: The bloom is off the John Harbaugh rose.
articles.body:
A few years ago, John Mara warned Head Coach Brian Daboll after his surprising first season as Giants head coach that it doesn't take long to go from Bono to Bozo. Daboll found out how true that was the next season and beyond. John Harbaugh has something much closer to Bono's portfolio, and his team's resounding opening week victory over Dallas had fans singing, "It's a beautiful day." But in the NFL, it's what have you done for me lately? Would Giants fans be singing again after facing the Super Bowl-contending Los Angeles Rams , or would they be saying, "I still haven't found what I'm looking for"?

Bozo it is. The Rams brought the Giants back down to earth with a 28-6 victory that wasn't as close as the score indicated. What did we learn from this thrashing?

The Rams' defensive line wasted no time letting the Giants' offensive line know what a real pass rush looks like. The Giants took the opening kickoff, and they did move the ball for a little while, but only in fits and starts. Right from the start, Dart felt pressure. He did complete a (poorly thrown) pass to Isaiah Likely , who made a nice adjustment for a 5-yard gain, and on the next play Dart went to Malachi Fields with another poorly thrown pass for 14 yards that Fields made a great play on to catch. That's the sign of a quarterback who is afraid to step into his throws. After an incompletion to Theo Johnson (a recurring theme tonight and in every game, it seems) and a short Skattebo gain, Dart threw long but incomplete to Theo again. He had an excuse for that, though, because both Andrew Thomas and Jermaine Eluemunor were beaten, by edge defenders Josaiah Stewart and Byron Young . The Rams' rushers made a Dart sandwich and Dart's knee was pushed inward, causing him to leave the game.

Overall the Rams pressured Dart on half of his dropbacks, and that was without Aaron Donald doing very much…except stopping Skattebo near the goal line the one time the Giants threatened. Of course the double teams he faced helped the rest of the Rams' defensive line win their one-on-one battles. The Giants used to have a guy called Dexter Lawrence who did that. As a result of this, the pressure wasn't just coming from the outside. It came up the middle too, so much so that after Jameis Winston entered the game he looked afraid to really step into his throws, leaving many of them short. This wasn't the good Jameis we saw in Detroit last year. It was the bad Jameis, short-arming and throwing right to defenders.

Getting beaten by the Rams' defensive line wasn't restricted to the passing game. The Giants rushed 21 times, for only 52 yards. Cam Skattebo did his best trying to bounce off the first defender to hit him, but he only gained 36 yards on 12 rushes. Najee Harris , seeing his first action, gained only 6 yards in four carries. Inexplicably, offensive coordinator Matt Nagy had him in there carrying the ball the one time the Giants got inside the 10 instead of Skattebo. On third-and-2, Harris was tackled for a loss by Aaron Donald.

And this suggests what might be a theme for the entire season. This is not a Giants team that is built to play from behind. Last week they were able to dictate to the Dallas defense, stay ahead of them most of the night, and use the running game to grind the Dallas defense down. Falling behind early against the Rams, we saw that the Giants' receivers didn't get open much. It didn't help that Winston was short-arming the ball or throwing off his back foot, but this looks like a team that needs to win the first half to thrive.

The game is won in the trenches. Part II

Correct me if I'm wrong, but I believe the Giants were supposed to have a fearsome pass rush this season. Abdul Carter did get one sack, but that was it. Matthew Stafford was able to sit back there in the pocket and look at tourist photos from Australia if he'd wanted to. Meanwhile, the Rams' running backs carried the ball 24 times for 164 yards. Much of it early on was between the tackles, but as the game wore on, the Giants' old problems of setting the edge reared their ugly head again. To make matters worse, Brian Burns came off the field with an ankle injury late in the game.

Was Dennard Wilson the defensive coordinator tonight, or did they bring Shane Bowen back?

The inability to get to Stafford, or even put pressure on him on a consistent basis, led to the realization of the Giants' worst fear…

The Giants' secondary is not up to the task

Granted, any secondary is up against it when the pass rush doesn't pressure the quarterback. But the Rams' receivers, even with Puka Nacua sidelined, embarrassed the Giants' secondary. Davante Adams had 8 receptions in 10 targets for 195 yards and 2 TDs, and on most of them he was so wide open it was ridiculous. Tight end Terrance Ferguson caught six balls in nine targets. There were occasional good plays, including another interception plus two forced fumbles by Jevon Holland , and even passes defensed by Tyler Nubin and Greg Newsome II , but more often, Rams receivers were catching the ball with no Giant within five yards of them. In particular, when you see Adams downfield and Nubin the one defending, you know it's not going to end well.

The secondary gets a bit of a pass because Deonte Banks and Paulson Adebo were out with injuries, but it's not as if either one is considered a Pro Bowl threat. The bottom line is that any game in which the Giants' front seven does not dominate this season is probably going to be a loss.

After making all 4four extra points in his first game, kicker Dominic Zvada made both of his field goal attempts tonight, including a 52-yarder, and both were pretty much down the middle. Meanwhile, Jordan Stout averaged 52.5 yards on his (unfortunately) six punts, three of them inside the 20 and one of them for 78 yards. Hopefully there will be games this season in which they can be a factor in a Giants win. That may be as soon as next week, when the Giants face a Titans team that was looked at as an easy W but which doesn't look that way anymore.

articles.title: Studs and duds from Rams' bounce-back win vs. Giants
articles.summary: Without Puka Nacua and Myles Garrett, several Rams players stepped up in a big way on Monday night.
articles.body:
No Puka Nacua , no Myles Garrett , no problem?

Not exactly. The Los Angeles Rams still need both of those superstars if they're going to win a Super Bowl, but they looked pretty darn good without them on Monday night. The Rams cruised to a 28-6 victory over the Giants , earning their first win of the season under the lights at SoFi Stadium.

And in the absence of Nacua , Garrett and even Kamren Kinchens , several players stepped up. Davante Adams went off with a spectacular performance, as did Trent McDuffie and Matthew Stafford , among others. Here are our studs and duds from Monday's win.

It was a vintage performance by Adams against the Giants on Monday night. He caught eight passes for 195 yards and two touchdowns, coming up just 11 yards shy of his career-high of 206. The passes he caught weren't all easy, either. In fact, most of them were incredibly difficult to make. He had a 31-yard touchdown, a 64-yard reception on a deep ball and a terrific 27-yard grab before halftime to set up a field goal attempt.

He was by far the best player on offense for the Rams.

How good has McDuffie been thus far? He's been worth every penny (and pick) the Rams paid to get him, looking his best on Monday against New York. He had four total passes defensed, including his first interception as a member of the Rams. He was sticky in coverage, physical as a tackler and has looked every bit like the All-Pro the Rams thought he'd be in L.A.

Lake was peppered with targets in Week 1 and held up fairly well in coverage, despite giving up some completions. The Giants went after him early, too, but Lake responded with some excellent plays. He drove on the ball and nearly came away with an interception in the first quarter, broke up a pass intended for Isaiah Likely over the middle and also forced a fumble on Cam Skattebo that went out of bounds. He finished second on the team with six tackles, three passes defensed and the forced fumble.

Without Myles Garrett, Young had to step up as the Rams' top edge rusher. And he delivered with a terrific performance. He had five tackles, including a sack, along with three quarterback hits and a tackle for a loss. He was constantly around the quarterback throughout the night, whether it was Jaxson Dart or Jameis Winston . And his speed was on full display when he chased down Jameis from behind for the sack.

This was more like the Stafford we saw last season rather than the one we saw last week. He completed 22 of 31 passes for 327 yards and four touchdowns with one interception. The pick was undeniably bad, forcing a deep shot to Adams down the field, but he was otherwise sharp. Oh, and he didn't have his top receiver, Puka Nacua. He leaned heavily on Adams and Terrance Ferguson , who caught 14 of his 22 completions and accounted for 249 of his 327 yards.

Smith could be in danger of losing his job as the punt returner. He fielded a punt at his own 8-yard line and then retreated, losing 2 yards on the return by going down at the 6. To open the third quarter, he muffed the kickoff and couldn't corral it, gaining just 7 yards on the return and only getting to the 11-yard line. He didn't catch a pass on offense, either. The one bright spot was a 19-yard return on a punt where he had a ton of space to work because it was booted 78 yards downfield.

How much does Sean McVay really trust Mevis? He missed a 43-yard field goal after a perfectly executed 40-yard drive in 22 seconds before halftime. Then later on in the game, the Rams had a chance to try a 56-yard field goal but instead opted to take a delay of game and punt it away. It was with 7 seconds left in the half, so maybe McVay didn't want to give the Giants a shot at trying a Hail Mary, but still.

He's only attempted two 50-plus-yard field goals in his career, and it's reasonable to think McVay may not trust him very much to try long kicks – despite him clearly having the leg strength.

articles.title: Drew Gilbert's homer and 2-run single lead Giants past Twins 5-2 to end 3-game losing streak
articles.summary: Drew Gilbert homered and hit a two-run single, leading the San Francisco Giants past the Minnesota Twins 5-2 on Monday night to snap a three-game losing stre...
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Drew Gilbert homered and hit a two-run single, leading the San Francisco Giants past the Minnesota Twins 5-2 on Monday night to snap a three-game losing streak.

Brett Harris singled in a pair of runs for San Francisco in the first inning and Gilbert did the same in the second before leading off the fifth with his 11th homer.

Brooks Lee homered to begin the fourth against Giants starter Blade Tidwell , who exited after one more batter because of elbow discomfort. He will undergo tests Tuesday.

Tidwell was coming off his first win with the Giants and second of his career last time out at St. Louis .

Tristan Beck (1-0) relieved and pitched 2 2/3 scoreless innings for the win. Trent Harris worked the ninth for his second save.

Bo Davidson had his first career hit and stolen base in the first — becoming the first Giants player to get a hit and steal a base in his major league debut since Red Tramback on Sept. 15, 1940.

The Giants opened their season-ending homestand, which concludes against the rival Los Angeles Dodgers this weekend, with their third victory in 10 games. They were swept by the two-time defending World Series champion Dodgers last weekend in Los Angeles.

Emmanuel Rodríguez homered in the eighth for the Twins.

Minnesota right-hander Zebby Matthews (9-11) struck out nine — his second-most this season behind 10 on July 31 at Seattle — and didn't walk a batter. He allowed five runs and eight hits over five innings.

Twins RHP Taj Bradley (11-6, 3.81 ERA) pitches the middle game of the series Tuesday night opposite Giants RHP Anthony Molina (3-1, 4.18).

articles.title: Flacco tells Joe Burrow he thought Ja'Marr Chase TD was 'uncatchable'
articles.summary: There were some great reactions on the Cincinnati Bengals' sideline to receiver Ja'Marr Chase's remarkable touchdown catch.
articles.body:
There were some great reactions on the Cincinnati Bengals ' sideline to receiver Ja'Marr Chase's remarkable touchdown catch in a win against the Houston Texans , as revealed in an "Inside the NFL Week 2 Mic'd Up" video shared by the NFL's Twitter/X account .

"That's unbelievable," quarterback Joe Burrow told Chase.

"I ain't gonna lie," Chase said to teammate Tee Higgins . "I didn't think he was throwing that. … I had to slow down and wait for it. I couldn't see the ball. And then I was running with him in front of me. That ended up working perfect right there."

Cincinnati Bengals vs. Houston Texans, photos from NFL Week 2

"We thought that ball was like a little bit - we thought it was like kind of uncatchable," backup quarterback Joe Flacco told Joe Burrow. "The next thing you know, boom, it was perfect."

"I literally don't know what I did," Chase told reporters after the game, per The Enquirer's Kelsey Conway . "I couldn't see the ball for a second and I was just fighting, trying to get in position. But by the time I (saw) the ball, it was like in a light, and it came real fast. It was just adjustment."

articles.title: Kahleah Copper scores 16 of her 31 in 4th quarter and the Mercury rally past the Wings 87-86
articles.summary: Kahleah Copper scored 16 of her 31 points in the fourth quarter, including a go-ahead layup with 2.4 seconds left, and the Phoenix Mercury rallied to beat th...
articles.body:
PHOENIX (AP) — Kahleah Copper scored 16 of her 31 points in the fourth quarter , including a go-ahead layup with 2.4 seconds left, and the Phoenix Mercury rallied to beat the Dallas Wings 87-86 on Monday night.

A foul call against Phoenix was overturned with 13.3 seconds left in the fourth quarter, and the Mercury secured the jump ball. Then, Alyssa Thomas found Copper on a backdoor cut along the baseline to take the lead. Phoenix forced a difficult shot at the buzzer as Paige Bueckers ' 3-point attempt did not hit the rim.

Thomas finished with 15 points, 12 assists and 11 rebounds for her fifth triple-double of the season for Phoenix (16-27), which trailed 74-63 early in the fourth.

Dallas (26-17), which led by as many as 14 points, had a six-game winning streak snapped with its first loss since Aug. 17. The Wings remain tied for sixth place in the WNBA standings.

Bueckers scored 30 points to go with seven assists, and Jessica Shepard had 17 points and 19 rebounds for Dallas. Bueckers, who reached 30 points for the fourth time this season, set a Dallas record for points in a season with 853.

Dallas guard Arike Ogunbowale sank a baseline jumper — just her second basket of the game — with 1:43 left in the fourth for an 81-77 lead. After Phoenix scored the next four points to tie it, Bueckers was left open on the wing for a shot from well behind the arc for an 84-81 lead.

Dallas was just 14 of 21 from the free-throw line.

Wings: At Seattle on Wednesday in the final regular-season game for both teams.

Mercury: Host Las Vegas on Thursday to conclude the regular season.

articles.title: Quinn Gray Jr. gives honest reaction to rough season start
articles.summary: Heading into Week 3, Florida A&M sits at 1-3. After an impressive opening win against Quinn Gray’s former program, Albany State, the Rattlers have suffered t...
articles.body:
Heading into Week 3, Florida A&M sits at 1-3. After an impressive opening win against Quinn Gray's former program, Albany State, the Rattlers have suffered three straight losses to South Carolina State, Miami, and Tennessee State.

Speaking about the tough stretch on the SWAC Coaches' Call, Gray says he understands and expected the job of restoring Florida A&M to its former glory to be tough. Gray has already dealt with grave injuries to key contributors this season.

Transfer Isaiah Knowles suffered a season-ending injury in the Orange Blossom Classic against South Carolina State, and backup quarterback Dustin Fletcher, who served as QB1 for the Rattlers following Knowles's injury, also suffered an injury against Tennessee State on Saturday.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Asked whether the pressure and expectations of leading Florida A&M have matched what he anticipated when he took the job, Gray made clear nothing has caught him off guard.

"No, that's exactly what I expected. There's nothing about this job that hasn't been what I expected. I know what this job is all about. I'm a Rattler. I know what the expectation is."

Gray pointed to correctable mistakes, rather than a lack of effort, as the difference between Florida A&M's record and where it could be.

"Our kids are going out there playing and trying to put their best foot forward," Gray said. "There's just some mistakes that we've made that have kept us out of the winning column."

He described the relationship between coaching staff and players as a shared responsibility.

"At the end of the day, they have a responsibility of performing, and we have a responsibility of putting them in the right situation to be successful," he said.

Gray also said coaches must be willing to examine their own performance when the team falls short.

"If we can't get it done, then we as coaches have to look at ourselves, and then also the players have to look at themselves to make sure that they're putting their best foot forward as well," he said.

He also reaffirmed his commitment to putting in the necessary work heading into Saturday.

"You won't hear any complaints from us," he said. "We're going to do what it is that we have to do to try and get our guys ready to play on Saturdays."

articles.title: Recap: Avs bested by Winnipeg in second preseason contest
articles.summary: An AHL-riddled roster falls to the Jets, 3-1.
articles.body:
The Colorado Avalanche and Winnipeg Jets met at Canada Life Center in Downtown Winnipeg for a preseason matchup. Winnipeg held on to a 3-1 win, but against an Avalanche squad that sent just 8 opening-night-roster-level players.

Things got off to a slow start, as this one definitely played out like a preseason game, with both squads not sending a full onslaught of talent onto the ice. Eventually, Gabriel Vilardi opened the scoring, with an assist from Isak Rosen and Vladislav Namestnikov .

Zachary L'Heureux couldn't play the puck effectively along the boards; it got caught behind the net, and once Christian Wolanin got it in the corner, two Jets converged on him. Isak Rosen won the puck, found Vilardi in the slot, and he fired it home.

Winnipeg's next mark came off the stick of Cole Perfetti , who did well to wait patiently at the back door as the Jets went low to high, found a streaking Mark Scheifele , and got it over to Perfetti for an easy goal. That made it 2-0 Jets after two periods of play.

Dylan Demelo 's point blast gave Winnipeg a commanding 3-0 lead in the third period, and Brett Kulak and Fabian Lysell finally helped Georgii Merkulov earn Colorado 's lone goal of the evening, bringing us to our final score of 3-1 Jets.

I was happy to see that Fabian Lysell had an apple on Colorado's lone tally. His arrival in Colorado has some interesting dynamics, but his skill is clear. I noticed at camp that Bednar was pretty active in communicating with Lysell, and if that can foster some maturity in Fabian, he could end up panning out.

Netminder Ilya Nabokov's stat line wasn't great, letting in two goals on just five shots. The group in front of him did well to limit the opportunities, but he couldn't have done much on Perfetti's goal. I'd imagine he'll keep getting ice time throughout the preseason so management can get a feel for his current capabilities in the North American game.

Only four of the players that were featured tonight for the Avalanche played in preseason game number one. It's pretty common for the big guns not to travel for a road preseason game, so I'd expect more NHL usuals to be featured on Friday when the Jets come to Ball Arena.

The Avalanche will get back to Colorado and, as mentioned, welcome the Winnipeg Jets to Ball Arena on Friday at 6:30 p.m. MT.

Let us know what you thought of this contest in the comments!

articles.summary: Penta and Roxanne Perez qualified for the 2026 Money in the Bank ladder matches on Raw. The full updated card, remaining spots and Friday's qualifiers.
articles.body:
The men and women's Money in the Bank ladder matches are two-thirds full after Monday Raw in San Antonio, Texas. Monday's episode saw Penta and Roxanne Perez punch their tickets into the match joining Bron Breakker, Je'Von Evans and Trick Williams on the men's side and Sol Ruca, Lola Vice and Jacy Jayne on the women's side. Here's the latest on the card. Let's talk wrestling.

ESPN App with ESPN Unlimited in the U.S., Netflix internationally

Bron Breakker, Je'Von Evans, Penta, Trick Williams

Sol Ruca, Lola Vice, Roxanne Perez, Jacy Jayne

All four remaining spots belong to SmackDown, since both Raw allocations are now filled. The next qualifiers come Friday: CM Punk vs. Gunther vs. Finn Balor on the men's side and Charlotte Flair vs. Giulia vs. Lash Legend on the women's side. Perez is the only woman in the current field with a previous Money in the Bank appearance.

Roman Reigns (c) vs. LA Knight, World Heavyweight Championship

Men's Money in the Bank Ladder Match: Bron Breakker vs. Je'Von Evans vs. Penta vs. Trick Williams vs. TBD vs. TBD

Women's Money in the Bank Ladder Match: Sol Ruca vs. Lola Vice vs. Roxanne Perez vs. Jacy Jayne vs. TBD vs. TBD

Results per WWE's Raw coverage, September 21, 2026.

Penta (replacing Solo Sikoa) vs. Dragon Lee vs. Dominik Mysterio

Roxanne Perez vs. IYO SKY vs. La Catalina

Penta's addition is the real story. After losing to Roman Reigns on last week's episode of Raw in Mexico City in one of the best matches of 2026, WWE is riding Penta's wave. He's so over right now, it would be foolish for WWE not to put him in the men's ladder match at MITB.

Perez's pin of IYO SKY says a few things. First, IYO is a pro's pro for putting Perez over. Second, WWE is finally giving Perez an opportunity to shine. She has it all and now she may be getting the chance to prove it.

Williams and Jayne are both champions already, which probably means neither of them will win their MITB matches. If one was to go over it would be Jayne. She is one of the most gifted and well-rounded performers on the women's side and the title picture could benefit greatly from her having the briefcase with the rest of Fatal Influence by her side.

The best thing about the still-building MITB ladder match fields is the amount of new faces. There's so much young talent in the matches already, it'll be interesting to see who fills out the last four spots.

Reigns-Knight could be an amazing main event. If Knight doesn't go over here, it'll be tough. Fans desperately want him to have his title reign and he just delivered the best mic work of his WWE career on Raw. Yeah, it's probably time.
